#1455. Arsenal vs Man City: The remarkable statistic that exposes Enzo Maresca's biggest challenge at the Emirates

By Naim Beneddra | 28 Nov 2026 12:10

Manchester City will travel to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday knowing that defeat against Arsenal would leave them nine points behind the reigning Premier League champions, and Enzo Maresca's side may find themselves with little margin for error in front of goal.

One particularly striking statistic illustrates the challenge awaiting the Citizens: they have missed 28 big chances in the Premier League this season, exactly as many as Arsenal have created in their opening 11 matches.

Mikel Arteta's side have nevertheless established a six-point advantage over City, largely thanks to a defensive record that remains comfortably superior to that of their title rivals.

City have created 40 big chances in the Premier League this season, a tally bettered only by Brighton & Hove Albion (44).

Their overall attacking numbers remain encouraging. Maresca's men have scored 22 goals from 22.19 expected goals (xG), suggesting that their finishing across all types of chances has broadly matched expectations.

Premier League 2026/27, after 11 matchdays

Both teams have played 11 games. The best figure in each row is highlighted; bar length is proportional to the highest value in the row. In the cards, negative values for goals conceded indicate better-than-expected defending; for goals scored, an underperforming attack. Data up to 25/11/2026.

Against Arsenal, however, City cannot necessarily count on generating the same volume of opportunities, particularly if their recent struggles in front of goal continue.

Erling Haaland has failed to score in his last three Premier League appearances, having found the net nine times in his opening eight games of the campaign. The Norwegian has attempted 12 shots and accumulated 2.0 xG during that barren run.

There is nevertheless reason for encouragement for the visitors. Haaland has scored in each of his last four Premier League encounters with Arsenal and could become only the fourth player to score in five successive appearances against the Gunners in the competition.

City's ability to supply their leading goalscorer in dangerous areas will be particularly important against an Arsenal side who have conceded just seven goals in 11 league fixtures.

Arsenal have won all five of their home Premier League matches this season, scoring 10 goals and conceding just twice. Their ability to protect slender advantages has been particularly important, with four of their nine league victories coming by a 1-0 scoreline.

According to Opta, the Gunners concede chances worth just 0.70 xG per 90 minutes when leading, compared with 0.77 when drawing and 1.10 when trailing.

Those figures underline the importance of the opening goal for Maresca's side. Allowing Arsenal to take the lead could force City into prolonged periods of possession against a compact defensive structure, with increasingly limited space for Haaland to operate in.

Individual quality could prove decisive in such circumstances. City average a league-high 11.3 successful dribbles per game, compared with Arsenal's 6.2, and the ability of players such as Jeremy Doku to beat their markers could help the visitors disrupt Arteta's defensive organisation.

There have, however, been signs of vulnerability from the champions over the past week. Arsenal surrendered leads against both Newcastle United and Borussia Dortmund, while David Raya's fitness remains a concern ahead of Sunday's encounter. Arteta has also been assessing his first-choice goalkeeper's availability.

City have gone four Premier League matches without a victory after winning their opening seven fixtures, and their attacking numbers suggest that Maresca still has the personnel to trouble the champions.

The difficulty will be making the most of those opportunities against opponents who have repeatedly demonstrated this season that a single goal can be enough to secure all three points.

#1454. Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan: Five things we learned – a breakout night and a glaring issue

AC Milan went into their Europa League fixture against Olympiacos in need of a win to get the ball rolling, and win they did.

The eventual 2-4 scoreline only tells part of the story, as Ruben Amorim’s side had to battle back from two goals down. Lorenzo Pirola’s header drew what was officially an own-goal from Mike Maignan, then Jota Silva doubled the lead after a slack pass from Koni De Winter was punished.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the Omari Hutchinson show. The Englishman gave Milan hope with a wonderful solo goal, before turning provider for Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to complete the turnaround. Diego Moreira’s late goal on the counter made sure of a very important three points.

So, the Diavolo return to Italy with smiles on their faces, cultivating the hopes of a play-off spot and keeping the top eight dream alive too. Ivan Stoev has picked out five major talking points from a dramatic night on the outskirts of Athens.

Omari Hutchinson has had mixed performances when given the opportunities since his arrival in the summer and the feeling is that he had plenty of work to do in order to justify the hefty optional price tag on his loan contract. Games like the one against Olympiacos are just the type of opportunities for the attacker to prove his abilities.

The Nottingham Forest loanee didn’t get off to the best start as Milan struggled in the opening 45 minutes with their opponents pressing very high and aggressively. This starved him of possession in a central role and he didn’t get the ball to his feet much, let alone with space to run at.

In the second half, however, Hutchinson moved to a wider role on the right flank and he immediately started causing trouble for the Greeks.

In the 56th minute it was an impressive solo run by the Englishman that started Milan’s comeback as the winger picked up the ball in his own half and carried it all the way to the opponent’s penalty box, before cutting onto his left foot and beating the keeper with a tidy finish in the far post.

Milan fez uma grande reviravolta na segunda parte em casa do Olympiacos, com Omari Hutchinson em destaque. https://t.co/RsOgYVqrP7

Seven minutes later Hutchinson continued to cause trouble down that flank. This time around he found Cisse with a lovely cross and the youngster made no mistake to bury it and bring the scores level.

The former Arsenal academy man wasn’t finished yet though: in the 71st minute he provided yet another inviting cross into the penalty box which found Pulisic, who applied a lovely volleyed finish to make it 3-2.

Hutchinson then continued to be a menace in transition as he showed relentlessness even in the dying minutes. A corner was cleared and he picked up possession, somehow beat a man and ran with it, getting the ‘hockey assist’ for Moreira’s goal.

It was an absolutely brilliant second-half performance and if he finds continuity then that option to buy might just before more appealing, or at the very least a re-negotiation to keep him permanently. The issue is that the Olympiacos owner also owns Forest, and he saw that display first-hand.

The goals Milan conceded were quite preventable yet again. The feeling is definitely growing as January approaches that the back line needs a true leader in the middle of a defence that continues to be error-prone.

Mario Gila has looked like a bargain of a signing and he has been superb, but he is playing mostly as a right-back/outside centre-back. Strahinja Pavlovic remains a key player as well, but the same applies as with Gila just on the left side.

Koni De Winter is just not a man that you can trust to anchor the rearguard to a high level most weeks. He’s had some stellar performances – the game against Inter comes to mind – but he often follows up those performance with some shocking ones.

Matteo Gabbia is definitely better in terms of leadership and keeping things tidy, but we will need to wait and see if he features in Amorim’s long-term plans. He’s been injured for quite a while too, so a reacclimatisation period will be required.

Sankhoun Diawara also looked very shaky in Greece, but this in itself proves a point because the idea cannot have been for him to start as many games as he has. It just further signals that someone who can play down the middle and steady everything could be the difference this season and beyond.

Ardon Jashari got his first Milan goal at the weekend in the win over Frosinone. Then, the unfortunate injury to Luka Modric leading up to the Olympiacos game meant he was given the chance to prove himself, after a few shaky performances this season.

Excluding a few misplaces passes in the first half, the Swiss international was solid enough. There wasn’t anything flashy but also no errors leading to goal, which was a relief.  The stats say that he had 77 touches, completed 58/64 passes (91%), had 1 big chance created, 2 tackles, 7 recoveries and 1 clearance. He also won 2/2 aerial duels and 2 ground duels, committing just 1 foul.

Speaking of chances being seized, it’s worth giving a shoutout to Fikayo Tomori who came on for a struggling De Winter. Milan looked much more solid with the Englishman on the pitch as he showcased his athleticism but also his experienced reading of the game.

The professionalism shown by Tomori must be respected given the centre-back was excluded from the squad in the summer and put on the transfer market. He worked hard to prove that he deserves to stay and to play. Now, the next mission is to earn what currently seems like an unlikely renewal.

In the first half Milan were struggling with the high press and the limited space, so they had limited chances going forward. The second half was a completely different story especially with Yunus Musah and Pulisic coming on for Estupinan and Goncalo Ramos.

We have already mentioned Hutchinson ran the show, but Pulisic was also crucial as he scored an impressive volley which is hard to execute by any standard,  and he then goal the assist that made the final 4-2. He should’ve really scored another one, but we’ll give him a well-earned pass.

Moreira was also heavily in the mix and at times he was frustrating with his end product being lacking, though the direct nature of his pace and dribbling were a joy to watch again. Having a player who picks up the ball and says ‘Fine, I’ll do it’ is really refreshing. His defensive effort as a wing-back was not lacking either.

Cisse all in all had a quiet game yet found his name up in lights on the scoreboard for a 10th time this season with a tidy headed finish. The knack that he has for being in the right place at the right time is something that is so impressive in a 20-year-old. A pay rise could be on the way to fend off calls from England.

We have to give the coach his flowers too, don’t we. The first half wasn’t good but it was still better compared to some other European performances this season. The goal was very preventable, but the Rossoneri did well not to fold under the pressure Olympiacos were applying.

In the second half the coach made two changes which improved the team quite a bit, though one of them was forced as Ramos was injured. Amorim revealed after the game that he knew the Greek side couldn’t keep up their high press for 90 minutes, which would yield spaces to attack in the second half.

Shifting Hutchinson to the right was also the correct choice, as was taking off De Winter for Tomori, and also letting Cisse play as a centre-forward. Depending on how Ramos is, he might have to do the same in Cagliari.

Finally, it is worth mentioning the attitude was completely different as opposed to the game against Ferencvaros. The desire and belief that the game could be turned around offers some encouragement that this team cannot just get into the knockout stages, but can give anyone a game if they show up.

#1453. Brazil’s dominance in the Copa Libertadores is "unprecedented," as plans to include MLS and Mexico emerge (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 12:23

Brazilian clubs are enjoying "unprecedented dominance" of the Copa Libertadores, according to South American football expert Tim Vickery in an exclusive Sports Mole interview.

Palmeiras will face Estudiantes in Saturday's Copa Libertadores final at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, aiming to make it eight Brazilian winners in a row.

The run began with Flamengo in 2019, and five of the last seven finals have been all-Brazilian affairs, most recently when Flamengo beat Palmeiras 1-0 last year. That victory also drew Brazil level with Argentina on 25 Libertadores titles apiece.

Speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, Vickery explained why the balance of power in South America has shifted so dramatically.

"Nothing like this has ever happened before. This is unprecedented dominance, and it's fairly easy to explain," Vickery said.

"The big reason behind all of this is money. The Brazilian clubs are far richer than even the giants from Argentina. But the financial distance was massive a decade ago, and the Brazilians weren't dominant then.

"There have been some other developments, especially the influx of Portuguese coaches. The run began in 2019 with Flamengo and Jorge Jesus, and Abel Ferreira of Palmeiras has already won this title twice. It's clearly brought the Brazilian domestic game up another level.

"Brazilian clubs are also far better at scouting the other South American countries. Bringing someone in strengthens the Brazilian league, and even if the player doesn't come off, it weakens the league he's come from."

Change may be on the way at home. Brazilian clubs can currently name nine foreign players per match, but that limit will be cut gradually from 2027 until it reaches five in 2030.

"I wonder if that might level the playing field just a little bit," Vickery added. "But in general terms, it's hard to see Brazil not being dominant unless there is some kind of Pan-American thing.

"We saw in the Club World Cup last year that sides from Major League Soccer can be competitive. Botafogo beat Seattle, but I thought Seattle were probably better.

"The main problem is the map. The distance from Buenos Aires to Mexico City is further than that between London and Mumbai, and the calendar makes it difficult.

"But there's an obvious synergy. Major League Soccer is a new product that lacks tradition, and therefore credibility. The South American club game has so much of both. In one way or another, there will be more Pan-American moves in the future. Watch this space."

Estudiantes, meanwhile, are seeking their fifth Copa Libertadores crown after triumphing in the 1968, 1969, 1970 and 2009 editions.

#1451. Liverpool transfer news: La Liga club in 'contact' with Kostas Tsimikas ahead of Reds exit

By Saikat Mandal | 28 Nov 2026 12:34

La Liga outfit Villarreal are reportedly showing keen interest in signing Liverpool defender Kostas Tsimikas.

The 30-year-old joined the Reds in the summer of 2020, signed by then-manager Jurgen Klopp, and has since made 124 appearances for the club across all competitions.

Tsimikas, who was mostly used as a back-up for Andrew Robertson, has never truly established himself as a regular starter and spent last season on loan at AS Roma.

The Greece international has made just one start in the Premier League this season, while a further three appearances have come off the bench, totalling 76 minutes.

The left-back has featured more regularly in cup competitions, making four Champions League appearances and starting three of them.

According to a report from SPORT24, Villarreal are showing strong interest in the defender and are closely monitoring his situation.

Tsimikas is under contract at Anfield until the end of the season and is widely expected to leave the club on a free transfer next summer.

The report claims that the Yellow Submarines have already made contact with the player's representatives, with the discussions understood to have been positive.

Villarreal are reportedly exploring the possibility of reaching an agreement, believing that Tsimikas possesses the qualities and experience they are looking for to strengthen the left side of their defence.

The defender has won one Premier League title, two EFL Cups and one FA Cup with Liverpool, proving to be a reliable squad player during his time at the club.

Milos Kerkez is the first-choice left-back under Andoni Iraola, and Liverpool should look to find a quality replacement for Tsimikas next summer.

The Reds have been linked with a move for New England Revolution defender Peyton Miller, who is widely tipped to secure an eye-catching move to a major European club in the future.

#1450. Russell must do something wacky now after disappointing Bahrain GP qualifying

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”

This was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”

No. 1 ☝️#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/01PqrckQS9

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”

“Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. “The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”

We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”

A reminder that Isack Hadjar will drop from third to eighth after his grid penalty.

QUALIFYING CLASSIFICATIONCan't wait for Sunday! 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/qqi8hPDcKA

“It is fantastic. We have been trying many grand prix to get pole. Sometimes a bit closer than others but to finally get it, from where we started the season, pretty incredible. I am happy with today and, for sure, I am going to try and win tomorrow. When you start first, that is the target.”

Big disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

*Hadjar’s three-place grid penalty will drop him down to eighth place for the race tomorrow.

Neither of the Red Bulls can improve in the first sector but it is those behind them who need significant improvements. The two Ferraris are going along nicely at the start of their final flying laps. Hadjar is unable to improve despite a purple final sector. Verstappen then goes fastest in the final sector and improves his advantage at the top.

Hamilton meanwhile went fastest in the middle sector and goes second fastest overall. Piastri cannot improve but stays ahead of Russell.

Norris is the final man across the line but is only fast enough for P6. That means that Verstappen takes pole in Malaysia, which is the first time this season that Red Bull have taken pole position. Hamilton is second with Hadjar third, although the Frenchman has a five-place grid penalty.

MAX VERSTAPPEN TAKES POLE FOR THE BAHRAIN GRAND PRIX IN MALAYSIA!! 👊#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/NgtaCAZacL

The two Red Bulls, who are one and two at the moment, will be the first two drivers across the line on these final efforts.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

The championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

Hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one new set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv

As the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

He has not set blistering first and second sector times but a purple final sector puts him into second and the Italian is safely into Q3.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

11. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)12. Carlos Sainz (Williams)13. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes)14. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)

Mercedes have put a brand new set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a big moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen currently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

17. Nico Hulkenberg (Audi)18. Oliver Bearman (Haas)19. Esteban Ocon (Haas)20. Alex Albon (Williams)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr

That has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a big lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

As it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac)

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he says Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

“Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and Q1 is officially under way. The two Haas drivers are the first to head out. Other than that, it is a quiet start to Q1.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change

Hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara currently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

“Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”

“It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

“The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”

Especially with the big upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso)

With Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car update since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

This race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

#1449. GdS: Vinicius, Roc Nation and a central role – Milan’s plan to land Endrick in €60m deal

AC Milan are not giving up on the idea of signing Endrick because they believe that the coup is possible, either in January or next summer.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report this morning that the positive results Ruben Amorim’s side have collected recently (five wins in the last six league games plus the Europa League victory in Athens) have not changed Gerry Cardinale’s mind about the need to strengthen the squad.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Brazilian’s name remains at the top of the list of targets for the attacking department, even though Mourinho reiterated yesterday that he wants ‘neither signings nor sales in January’. The Rossoneri hope that Endrick will push for a change of scenery to play more.

One assist could come from the player’s agents, who will reiterate this intention in the upcoming meeting with Florentino Perez and the management of Los Blancos. It’s unlikely that this will be enough to secure the green light, especially for a permanent exit.

However, in Madrid there is also another situation to monitor carefully: the one relating to Vinicius Jr. who – like Endrick – is represented by the American agency Roc Nation Sports.

Vinicius renewed his contract with Real Madrid last August, and his contract no longer expires on June 30th, but in 2032. His salary has also skyrocketed, going from €18m net to well over €20m per year.

The new deal was supposed to quell rumours of a departure from Madrid. Instead, after Saudi side Al Ahli first showed interest in him (putting in a huge bid which was rejected) and more recently Arsenal, it’s now the turn of speculation about PSG.

The long-term injuries that have sidelined Kvaratskhelia and Doué are leading Luis Enrique to consider the Brazilian option for the January transfer window. Vinicius doesn’t want to leave, despite his disappointing performances (only two goals) and Mbappé being the star man.

This is good news for Milan. Why? Because the sale of Vinicius would virtually eliminate Endrick’s chances of leaving.

The Roc Nation Sports team, therefore, have a lot to discuss with Florentino. They know it’s unlikely their two clients will be able to stay at Real Madrid beyond January.

With Rodrygo expected to return from his serious knee injury in early March at the latest by early 2027, the pressure on the attack will be even greater. Endrick has played just 160 minutes for Real Madrid so far, compared to 248 in his six matches with the Seleção between September and November.

Something isn’t right, and despite Mourinho’s words about not wanting to lose him and Endrick’s comments about not wanting to leave, it’s clear the 20-year-old can’t continue to watch his team-mates.

With Mbappé, Vinicius, Diomande, Arda Guler, Brahim Díaz, Espí and Bellingham in the squad – plus Rodrygo coming back – it’s difficult to imagine a lot of playing time.

Milan want to make use of their alliance with Roc Nation, the American sports and entertainment giant with which Cardinale and RedBird have long had business deals.

Furthermore, the CEO of the newly formed Milan Sports & Entertainment – the holding company that will consolidate RedBird’s current and future investments in Milan – is Brett Yormark, former Roc Nation executive. He is the brother of Michael Yormark, executive of Roc Nation Sports.

Milan would give Endrick a central role on and off the pitch: they would use him as a right-sided attacking midfielder in a 3-4-2-1 formation, but also as a centre-forward. They would also make a significant investment (€60m plus bonuses) to land him permanently.

A Nico Paz-style buy-back is possible. Milan want to get the deal done either in January or next summer, because Endrick, according to Cardinale is ‘one of the best in the world in his position’.

#1448. Goztepe SK vs Trabzonspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 28 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 13:00

Trabzonspor will move to the summit of the Turkish Super Lig table, at least for a couple of hours, if they extend their seven-match winning run in the division when they travel to Goztepe SK on Monday evening.

Thomas Reis's side sit second, three points behind leaders Galatasaray, while Stanimir Stoilov's side occupy 10th spot on 18 points after 12 games.

Having spent the last two seasons pushing for the European places, Goztepe have found life harder in 2026-27, although Stoilov's side have shown in recent weeks that they remain a dangerous proposition on their day.

The Izmir outfit strung together four straight league wins in October, beating Eyupspor, Kocaelispor and Corum before producing their standout result of the season, a 2-1 comeback victory at Fenerbahce in which Sinclair Armstrong and Andre Henrique struck two minutes apart late on.

That run was ended by a 2-1 home defeat to Istanbul Basaksehir before the international break, but Goztepe responded with a 1-0 success at Erzurumspor last time out.

The curious thing about Goztepe's campaign is how much better they have been away from home, having collected 14 of their 18 points on the road (W4, D2, L1), while their record in Izmir reads just one win, one draw and three defeats from five outings.

Stoilov's men will need to reverse that trend against a side who won 2-1 at this venue last December, when Ernest Muci scored twice, although Goztepe did hold Trabzonspor to a 1-1 draw at Papara Park in May and beat them 2-1 here in October 2024, the last time they won this fixture competitively.

Trabzonspor, meanwhile, have been transformed since Fatih Tekke left by mutual consent at the start of September, with the club sitting 11th at the time.

The Black Sea giants have now won nine of their 12 league games, losing just twice, and they arrive in Izmir on the back of seven successive Super Lig victories, the latest a 1-0 home win over Eyupspor courtesy of Ozan Tufan's fifth-minute header.

Defence has been the foundation of the revival, with Trabzonspor conceding only eight goals in 12 matches, the meanest record in the division, while their perfect home record (six wins from six) has been backed up by three wins from six on the road.

Reis's side also head into the weekend in high spirits after coming from behind to win 2-1 at CSKA Sofia in the Conference League on Thursday, with Mohamed Salah equalising before Noah Saviolo struck in stoppage time to lift them to nine points and eighth place in the league phase.

With Galatasaray facing Besiktas in the derby later on Monday night, victory would take Trabzonspor level on 31 points and above the champions on goal difference, piling the pressure on the Lions before they kick off.

Goztepe are sweating on the fitness of Andre Henrique, who picked up an injury in the win at Erzurumspor and is expected to miss Monday's contest.

The Brazilian's likely absence should see Stoilov pair top scorer Juan with Janderson in attack, with Armstrong set to begin among the substitutes.

Right-back Arda Okan Kurtulan is suspended, while Juan and midfielders Alexis Antunes and Matus are all one booking away from a suspension, so the hosts may need to tread carefully with their discipline.

As for Trabzonspor, Reis is expected to be without Aral Simsir and Tim Jabol-Folcarelli, who are both dealing with injury problems, while Okay Yokuslu and Ruslan Malinovskyi are also unavailable.

Arseniy Batagov and Franculino Dju have returned to training, but Stefan Savic and Ernest Muci remain fitness concerns ahead of the trip to Izmir, meaning neither is guaranteed to feature.

Paul Onuachu should lead the line for the visitors, with Mohamed Salah and Noah Saviolo expected to provide support from the wide positions.

Ozcimen; Taha, Godoi, Bokele; Yildirim, Rhaldney, Miroshi, Akonnor; Antunes; Juan, Janderson

Onana; Pina, Nwaiwu, Ozkacar, Cabral; Mendy, Fabinho; Salah, Saviolo, Muci; Onuachu

Goztepe have shown they can trouble the big sides, but their home form has been poor and they will be without Henrique's cutting edge in attack.

Trabzonspor may have one eye on Monday night's derby, but the league's tightest defence, a seven-game winning streak and firing attack should be enough for the visitors to grind out another win and go top.

#1447. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

#1446. Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 17:22 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 24 November 2026

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

But this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an issue which Arteta must urgently address.

It is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

He obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

One back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured

Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7.

Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6).

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

After the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more quickly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.

#1444. Romano: Bruno Fernandes could leave Man Utd despite extension – Milan must be ‘closely monitored’

The contract extension does not mean that Bruno Fernandes will remain at Manchester United beyond this season, with AC Milan watching on.

The news broke on Friday that United had activated their unilateral option for a one-year extension on Fernandes’ current contract. This means the Portuguese will no longer be able to join the club on a free transfer in June 2027, but his future is far from definitively tied to Manchester.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, Fernandes himself confirmed recently that talks over a new deal (and not just the club option) are on hold for the time being. In the meantime, Milan continue to be linked with a swoop for the former Sporting CP man, who Ruben Amorim knows well.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano provided an update on the situation and he confirmed that the Rossoneri are ones to watch. MilanNews transcribed the journalist’s words.

“We told this story about Bruno Fernandes last summer. First, Juventus made an attempt, then Milan made a forceful attempt. The player chose to stay in Manchester but never renewed his contract over the summer,” he said.

“He had significant offers, not just from Italy. Galatasaray reportedly offered a lot of money, while a year ago, Al-Hilal – in June 2025 – put crazy sums on the table. He had many different options, competitively and financially, but he chose to stay at United.

“He never renewed his contract, and today I saw many saying ‘Goodbye Italy’. I believe today’s renewal is more about Manchester protecting Bruno Fernandes’s asset, rather than good news about keeping the player longer.

“The club and the player have been talking about a contract renewal for months. But a renewal means one thing, the extension another. ‘Contract extended’ means extending the current contract for another year, as was the case with Bruno Fernandes. ‘New deal’, on the other hand, means signing a completely different one. That’s the difference.

“Today, United activates the clause for another year, which protects Bruno Fernandes’ rights, preventing him from signing for free with another team in January. United needed to do this because Bruno Fernandes’ new contract is anything but close.

“Today, the conversations are stalled: the player has put everything on hold for a reason. He wants to know what United will be like. Bruno wants time to decide, understand how things will go with Pochettino and what the project will be. This renewal protects United financially.

“But there’s a release clause – €65 million – in Bruno Fernandes’ contract. But given his age and the length of his contract, I think any potential price would be lower anyway. Given his relationship with United, if Bruno Fernandes were to decide to leave at the end of the season, this contract protects United from losing him for free, but it wouldn’t prevent his exit.

“The Portuguese’s future is far from decided. The economic dynamics of the transfer market are changing, but not that Bruno Fernandes hasn’t decided yet. If he renews, it will be a completely new contract. I always add his relationship with Amorim – I always want to point that out.

“Amorim and Bruno have a great relationship, they have the same agent. There’s enormous respect between the two: I would always keep Milan closely monitored. But it’s clear that what happens doesn’t depend on Milan. So, we’ll see.”

#1443. We asked AI to predict Arsenal vs. Man City - you will believe how it ends

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 13:23

Formerly a reunion between two erstwhile Etihad colleagues, Arsenal vs. Man City takes on a different feel this season, as the Premier League champions welcome the Sky Blues to the Emirates for the first time since Pep Guardiola's emotional departure.

Mikel Arteta has already got one over his old superior's successor this season, masterminding a 3-0 Arsenal win in the Community Shield over Enzo Maresca's men, who responded by winning each of their first seven Premier League matches in 2026-27.

However, a dramatic drop-off on Man City's part has allowed Arsenal to build up a six-point advantage at the summit of the Premier League table, although both sides have been held to draws in their last two games in all competitions.

The sports media world is awash with predictions and forecasts for Arsenal vs. Man City, but does the most advanced technology on the planet foresee another three-goal success for the Gunners.

Sports Mole asked AI to simulate Sunday's Premier League main event - powered by match and player data from the campaign so far - and here's how it played out.

While David Raya has not been officially ruled out of Arsenal vs. Man City amid his shoulder concern, AI expects Kepa Arrizabalaga to get the nod in the Gunners goal, while Enzo Fernandez is snubbed from the Sky Blues' XI as Ayyoub Bouaddi, Enzo Fernandez and Phil Foden start centrally.

However, an aggressive City start does not materialise into anything tangible, as Erling Haaland - scoreless in three Premier League games heading into Sunday's match - has just one half-chance saved by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

The Norwegian's opposite number Kai Havertz then makes the breakthrough with 36 minutes gone, latching onto a low Noni Madueke cross and poking home past Gianluigi Donnarumma from inside the six-yard box.

The German's strike continues his stellar streak against Man City, making it four goal involvements from his last four league games against the Citizens; three of his own and one assist.

Maresca's men fail to find an equaliser before the break, although their sustained periods of possession offer the travelling faithful hope ahead of the restart.

Arsenal's slow starts to second halves have been evident against the likes of Slavia Prague, Newcastle United and Borussia Dortmund in recent weeks, and such shortcomings are also exposed here.

Jeremy Doku is wreaking havoc on Jurrien Timber on the left-hand side, and the tricky Belgian attacker proves to be the catalyst for City's leveller in the 62nd minute.

Getting beyond his marker and driving to the byline, Doku delivers a cross on the money for Haaland, who gets the better of perpetual on-field rival Gabriel Magalhaes and steers a flicked header past Kepa.

The Scandinavian sensation scores for the fifth league game in a row against Arsenal while ending his three-match Premier League scoring drought, but City's leveller does not lead to a sustained shift in momentum.

Instead, Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard seize the initiative, and the latter gets an 82nd-minute corner spot on for Gabriel, who seals a 2-1 Arsenal victory with a customary corner header.

Both teams finish the game with 11 men on the field as Arsenal skipper Odegaard collects the man of the match prize, having been a driving force in the Gunners' successful push to go nine points clear of the charges-ridden Citizens.

#1442. Lazio lose Tavares and Sutalo for at least three weeks as Juventus chase 11-point gap

Defenders Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo hurt their hamstrings at Napoli, leaving unbeaten Serie A leaders Lazio short in defence. The setback hits Gattuso's back line just as Juventus return from the break chasing the leaders.

Lazio’s defence has suffered a double blow. Nuno Tavares and Josip Sutalo were both injured in the 1-1 draw at Napoli. The timing is awkward for the leaders, who resume their league campaign against Lecce on 21 November.

Exact recovery times will only be set once all clinical tests are complete. The early estimate is about 20 days for each player, Sky Sport Italia reported. On that timeline, both miss the home game against Lecce and could return for the trip to Torino on 28 November.

Not every report is that hopeful. Football Italia reported that the pair should miss both the Lecce and Torino games. Under that scenario, they hope to be available again in the first week of December. The match against Atalanta on 6 December is also in doubt.

Tavares has been a real attacking outlet this season. He has one goal and four assists in 11 Serie A games. He also has a long record of muscle injuries. Sutalo has made eight league appearances since joining on loan from Ajax on 22 August.

Lazio must now turn to their alternatives. Alfonso Pedraza, who joined from Villarreal in the summer, is the leading option at left-back. He has played 322 minutes across the league and Coppa Italia. Diogo Leite and Doekhi are competing to replace Sutalo in the middle.

The stand-ins inherit a strong record. Lazio have scored 25 goals and conceded 9 so far. Keeping that defensive record with a reshuffled back line is now Gattuso’s task.

Juventus know Lazio’s quality first-hand. Gattuso’s side won 3-0 in Turin earlier this season. That result still weighs on the table. Five wins, three draws and three defeats make up the Juventus record from their opening games.

— S.S.Lazio (@OfficialSSLazio) November 8, 2026

Two missing defenders will not close the gap on their own. They do, however, give Juventus a window in which the leaders are weaker than usual. Any dropped points by Lazio over the coming rounds would only count if Juventus take care of their own fixtures.

Those fixtures follow Lazio’s closely. Como v Juventus is scheduled for Sunday 29 November at 20:45, the day after Lazio’s game against Torino. Further ahead, Lazio’s aim is to have both defenders fit for the Rome derby on 13 December.

#1441. Sublime England thrash Croatia in best performance for a decade

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

England’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

The visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

Their new head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh

It was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

Gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof

Kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

These could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

The goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

Bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z

England were swarming all over Croatia. Saka crossed, Gordon took the ball down and turned it back for Bellingham to stab home.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M

Gordon, after twice being denied, got his goal – with another header, as against the Czechs. This time Jarell Quansah, back in ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold, delivered from the right and Gordon met it to score for the fourth successive game for England. Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

After the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

Saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

There’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,

An amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We showed the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

[Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.
