Good cross from Gudmundsson on the left dips perfectly for Stach to volley but Bogle can’t get out of the way. He is a prolific underlapper and pays the price here, blocking his team-mate’s shot.

Tanaka loses the ball in midfield and Arsenal pile forward but Leeds mass the ranks of their defence and block the path to goal until Justin is fouled to relieve the siege.

It’s the incisive, between-the-lines passes that Arsenal are currently lacking. Perhaps a bit of rustiness after such a long break between games?

Calafiori drives past Bogle and whips over a cross that is behind Havertz who has to backpedal to head it which robs his effort of power. Trafford drops to his knees to gather.

Lewis-Skelly holds off Stach but then throws up his arms as if flapping a cape and clocks Stach in the face. Leeds are awarded a free-kick.

Leeds’ offside trap has been functioning well and now Arsenal’s well-oiled one kicks in to catch Gudmundsson and Okafor.

Arsenal have been eager to play quick passes over the Leeds defence in these opening exchanges. Arteta’s side usually prefer to build up more slowly but they are looking for Havertz quite early. A consequence, perhaps, of Leeds pushing quite high up the pitch.

Okafor’s blistering 20-yard shot is deflected behind for a corner. The linesman’s flag was up because he said Calvert-Lewin had moved towards the ball in an offside position but the referee overrules him.

Justin heads the ball to Ampadu who plays a one-two with Stach then chips the ball 40 yards, a real up and under, for Calvert-Lewin to chase. Raya beats him to it.

Aresnal launch a counter up the right and the telepathy between White and Saka for once breaks down when White runs offside for a return pass. Elvedi was there to sweep up in any case.

Muharemovic reads the game well and snuffs out a long pass looking for Havertz, shifts the ball up to Calvert-Lewin who is grabbed round the waist by Gabriel and Leeds are awarded a free-kick in the centre-circle.

Saka, miles offside, takes on a cross that he should have headed with a leaping volley instead and Trafford saves at very close range. Slick work between Odegaard and Madueke to get the ball to Saka.

Both sides used the opportunity of the playing of The Angel to muster in huddles. Leeds kick off, attacking from right to left, going all the way back to Trafford standing outside his box and he clips a long pass up the right and Leeds are immediately penalised with the linesman’s flag.

Arsenal switch to their right and try to free Saka but Trafford comes out to kick it into touch.

Arsenal in red and white, Leeds in yellow and black. Ben White was looking round to see if there was anyone in the Leeds line he recognised from his excellent year’s loan with them but Marcelo Bielsa’s promotion heroes have all moved on now. In fact, with Illan Meslier, there are two at the Gunners and none at Elland Road.

Long international break, we recovered most of our players and have a point to prove after our last game.

Everyone is fit and ready to play but we have a very difficult opponent.

We know that today is one of the toughest tasks in European football. They have been the most consistent side in Europe for years. Especially after a warning shot in the last game, they will be on it today.

But we didn’t win our good start in the lottery we earned it. We travel here in confidence.

Brighton didn’t park the bus. They went for it and pressed Arsenal. You need to do this. You have to go for it. If you sit deep their individual quality is too good. The one thing is to have a plan and a theory but another to execute it.

Last season we faced one of the best sides in the world so we didn’t dwell on [those defeats]. If we are at our best we have a chance to compete for points.

There’s no doubt who the biggest threat to Arsenal’s defence will be today: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has four goals in six games in all competitions this season and is the top scoring Englishman in the league since the start of last season. He’s a player Arsenal once looked at signing, many years ago.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

#1416. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1415. GdS: The latest on Milan’s nine injured players as pre-Cagliari preparations continue

AC Milan are continuing preparations for Monday’s trip to face Cagliari, with Ruben Amorim hoping to recover some injured players.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write that yesterday’s training session – following the overnight return trip from Greece – did not provide any definitive updates regarding those who are currently in the treatment room.

Having navigated the trip to Athens with nine players unavailable, Ruben Amorim hopes that his team’s run of bad luck has finally come to an end. In the meantime, the coach received some positive news regarding Gonçalo Ramos.

He came off at half-time in Piraeus having taken a knock to the shin, but he is in less pain now. If these encouraging signs hold over the next 48 hours, Ramos should be available for Monday’s match in Cagliari.

As for the others, everyone is eager to return and help the team, though it is worth noting that Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze will not be back until 2027 as their issues are more serious.

Strahinja Pavlovic was sidelined by a bout of colic and is feeling better, though he has had very little training time since the derby. The Serbian is a fighter and is keen to be available in Sardinia, so he will likely board the flight with the squad, then Amorim will make a decision.

Francesco Camarda is also experiencing less pain following a knock to his right ankle and is on the road to recovery. Luka Modrić continues to work on addressing the discomfort in his right thigh and he should return against Parma, though could still make the bench on Monday.

Davide Bartesaghi is dealing with peritendinitis in his right leg and is also aiming for a return against Parma. If his condition shows positive signs today and tomorrow, a surprise appearance in Cagliari cannot be ruled out. Ruben Loftus-Cheek and Pietro Terracciano will require a few more days.

#1414. Kean’s new tibia injury rules former Juventus striker out of Como v Juventus

Moise Kean has broken down again in Como training, three weeks after treatment that was meant to fix his shin. The former Juventus striker is set to miss about two more months, so he will not face his old club on 29 November.

Moise Kean has suffered a new tibia injury in training with Como. The former Juventus striker is now undergoing further medical tests. Sky Sport Italia reported that he will be out for about two more months. That timeline rules him out of Como’s home game against Juventus.

Como’s statement of 17 November gave no recovery date. The club promised an update once more information was available.

The new problem follows a treatment that was meant to end his shin trouble. On 30 October, Como’s update described his treatment at the Cugat Institute in Barcelona as successful. The club put his recovery at about five weeks. His progress was to be reviewed every day.

That plan has now collapsed. Kean had been out since early October. The original injury came while he was playing for Italy against France on 2 October. That match was the first leg of a Nations League tie.

The setback is a heavy blow for Como. In Serie A, his outings for the club added up to 160 minutes. He has yet to score, including in his single Champions League game. He joined from Fiorentina on an initial loan, with an obligation to make the move permanent. At Fiorentina he scored 27 league goals in two seasons, 19 of them in 2024/25. Before that, he came through the Juventus academy.

Without him, Como will have to rely on Douvikas up front. The club may also look for a striker in January.

For Juventus, the news removes one threat from a crucial stretch. Como are their next opponents after Venezia. The game is the Sunday evening fixture a week later, in round 13 of Serie A. Kick-off is at 20:45.

Luciano Spalletti’s side need results. Juventus sit six points behind fourth place and have averaged just over 1.6 points per game, according to Corriere dello Sport. The paper sees the run of fixtures as decisive for the push for a Champions League place. It warns that dropping points against Venezia would force Juventus to win every remaining game of 2026 to stay in touch with the top four.

The schedule offers little respite after the trip to Como. Juventus host Udinese on 6 December and Monza on 14 December. They then travel to Roma on 19 December.

#1412. Capello praises Hutchinson and outlines why Milan are Scudetto contenders

Fabio Capello has questioned why Omari Hutchinson does not play more for AC Milan, analysing the comeback win against Olympiacos.

Among the leading experts on the subject of Scudetto battles, it’s always worth considering whether Capello considers Milan to be in the title race. The coach won Serie A five times, four of which were with the Rossoneri. He was also a LaLiga champion twice with Real Madrid.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

At the moment, Ruben Amorim’s side remain five points off Lazio who are in top spot, while they are below Roma and Inter too. A Champions League place is something that Milan will have to fight hard for, given that Como are keeping up the pressure.

Capello gave an interview to La Gazzetta dello Sport in which he gave his thoughts on various talking points linked to Milan, from the win on Thursday to the potential title fight.

“More than a new beginning, it was a restart. After the derby, it was the first time I thought: Milan is coming back. But then I had to correct myself; what I had seen and believed was lost immediately afterward. Now this new victory is a sign that the team can truly start again from here.”

It was team spirit that made Amorim say that this could have been the turning point, do you agree?

“Absolutely. Previously, there had been a Milan side that was unpredictable, relying mostly on individual play and less on the team. They return from Athens knowing they have a solid foundation and can emerge from difficulties with character. The opponent wasn’t at all comfortable.”

“After a truly awful first half, against a team buoyed by previous victories, there was a desire to turn the result around; they never gave up. The substitutions, like Pulisic, helped because we’re talking about players capable of making the difference.

“But everyone remained present and involved in the game, and it must be said that the goals conceded were due to individual errors, the first while marking, the second while supporting. Perhaps it had to happen to rediscover this spirit, which is and remains the most important element.”

“Why not? It helps build confidence, it makes you believe that you’re on the right path, that by playing a certain way you can achieve results. And then the standings speak for themselves and say that Milan are right there.

“If they play like this, they could give Roma and Inter a run for their money, who I see as the most qualified candidates. Lazio? They’re still ahead, but it’s a surprise. Milan could be the real contenders, they’ve chosen a path that could lead to the top.”

Hutchinson has proven to be a new weapon. Were you surprised?

“Actually, when I saw him on the pitch, I wondered why he didn’t always play. Against Olympiacos, he made the difference because they couldn’t get to him. The interesting thing is that he did everything while maintaining great clarity.

“It’s also true that you need the Pulisic of the situation, who knows how to strike the ball perfectly or serve a team-mate. Another positive aspect is his total lack of selfishness. I’ve never seen anyone who seems to say, ‘I’ll do it, I’ll shoot’. Rather, he looks for a team-mate.

“Going back to Hutchinson, he has speed and a change of pace, very important qualities in today’s football, something PSG teaches us.”

“Let’s leave it, he remains on another level, a conductor from a world apart.”

They scored four goals without Ramos. How do you replace him now?

“It was thought that Gonçalo could be decisive right away, but let’s give him time, let’s wait. Maybe now that the competition is increasing, he can stimulate him.

“It’s also true that he needs balls in front of goal, he scores in the final 10-12 metres and few of them have come to him. That’s why I justify him.”

“He always scores like a No.9, and I trust Silvio Baldini who says he can do it…”

“I liked Jashari in the middle. He played with personality when he had the ball and chased down the opponent when he didn’t. Rabiot is his usual self. I still wonder why Juve didn’t keep him. They need to improve in defence, especially in concentration.”

#1411. Marching on together, Ao? Leeds look to tie down Tanaka to a new deal after shining this season - with Dominic Calvert-Lewin also in extension talks amid Man United interest

By SIMON JONES and TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 14:08 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:18 EST, 25 November 2026

Leeds United are in advanced talks with Japan international Ao Tanaka over a new contract.

The 28-year-old midfielder is close to agreeing terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029 with his current contract due to expire in the summer of 2028.

Leeds have lost only 10 games out of the 66 Tanaka has started since joining the club from Fortuna Dusseldorf in 2024. He has had an impressive start to the current campaign, becoming a key figure in Daniel Farke's side, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They currently sit seventh in the table.

Leeds have already tied down Ethan Ampadu to a four-year deal while Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson all signed new contracts during the summer transfer window.

Talks are also expected to progress over a new deal for Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has been linked with a move to bitter rivals Manchester United as they look to bolster their striking department.

Discussing Tanaka's form ahead of their emphatic win over Chelsea at the weekend, Farke said: 'It was a big ask for him after spending many years on second-tier level in Germany or here in the Championship.

Ao Tanaka (left) is in advanced talks with Leeds United over signing a new contract until 2029

Leeds are also in talks with striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin over a new deal to stay at Elland Road

'Last season was his first year in the top league. I think he’d shown glimpses of his potential, but he needed to find a bit of consistency. I would agree that he is finding this during the season.

'It was not always a 10 out of 10 performance but I think it's important for a player, once you're mature, that on the weaker days you're still a six or a seven out of 10, and this is what he's doing.

'So perhaps even on the more challenging days, he's at least solid and plays first of all with good confidence, like he always does, but also with a seriousness to be consistent and to work for the team, also against the ball, strong in the duels.

'Still sometimes in decision-making and in front of goal he can be a bit calmer. But overall, I think he's on a really good path to mature more and more. And if you do this, then you become more and more important for us. And we're all happy that he is in such a shape at the moment.'

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 with two headers from Yan Couto crosses, moving back into fourth place on 26 points. Juventus visit next and trail the side holding the last Champions League place by eight points.

Como beat Cagliari 2-0 at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Saturday, 21 November 2026. Both goals were headers, and Yan Couto crossed for both of them. The result lifted Fàbregas’ side back into fourth place. That is the last Champions League place, and Juventus are the next visitors.

Ramón opened the scoring after 24 minutes. He met Couto’s cross from the right and headed past goalkeeper Caprile. Da Cunha, the captain, doubled the lead in the 56th minute. He headed in another Couto delivery from the centre of the area.

Fàbregas left Nico Paz and Perrone on the bench. The two Argentinians had rejoined the squad only hours before kick-off after international duty. Como play AEK in the Champions League on Tuesday. Even without the pair from the start, the hosts kept Cagliari out. Both men entered in the 57th minute, with Liberali and Milla making way respectively. It was Como’s first win since a defeat to Inter before the international break.

For Fàbregas, the performance was not perfect, but he was very pleased. Perrone had a minor problem, the coach explained, which ruled out a full 90 minutes for the midfielder.

Como have now won three Serie A home games in a row without conceding, which they last did in October and November 1984, according to Sportmediaset. Da Cunha has three goals in his last four games across Serie A and the Champions League. Fàbregas has never lost to Cagliari in five Serie A matches as a coach. He has won three of them and drawn two. Cagliari have lost each of their last four away league games. That is their first run of four straight away defeats in Serie A since November–December 2023.

Como have eight wins, two draws and two defeats from 12 games, according to Como 1907. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

In that table, Juventus’ record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 12. The gap to Como stood at eight points before Juventus’ game against Venezia.

#1407. Inter throw away three two-goal leads at Atalanta as Juventus stay eight points back

Inter drew 4-4 at Bergamo after leading 2-0, 3-1 and 4-2, and dropped to third behind Lazio and Roma. Juventus sit eight points behind them before Thursday's Europa League game with Omonia and Sunday's trip to Como.

Inter led 2-0, then 3-1, then 4-2 at the New Balance Arena on Sunday night. They still left Bergamo with a single point. The 4-4 draw with Atalanta left Chivu’s side third, three points behind leaders Lazio on 32 and now overtaken by Roma on 30.

Behind them, Milan have 27 and Como 26. Inter’s advantage over Juventus stands at eight points. The top of the table is spreading out, and Inter’s slip leaves three clubs within three points of each other at the summit.

Esposito gave Inter a two-goal cushion with his first two goals of the night. Elmas pulled one back for Atalanta on 35 minutes. Esposito restored the margin seven minutes after half-time to complete his hat-trick.

Atalanta played with a late change in goal. Sportiello started because Carnesecchi had to pull out during the warm-up. De Ketelaere cut the gap on 72 minutes. Four minutes later Zappacosta handled a Thuram shot on the goal line. Inter’s advantage was back to two goals once Sučić beat Sportiello with the resulting penalty.

De Ketelaere struck for a second time on 81 minutes. Bastoni’s handball then gave Atalanta a stoppage-time penalty, and Kessié converted it.

Chivu said his side had failed the exam in the final minutes. He called the result “two gifted points”. Esposito now has six goals this season, and no Inter player has scored more in Serie A.

Inter also lost Hakan Çalhanoğlu. He came off in the 33rd minute with a problem in the hamstring of his right thigh and is due to have tests on Tuesday 24 November, Sky Sport reported. He will miss Wednesday’s Champions League game against Stuttgart and Saturday’s league match with Genoa at San Siro. It is his second muscle injury of the season, after a layoff of about 20 days in September.

Juventus arrive at their own busy week in form. All four goals against Venezia came after half-time, from Woltemade, Koopmeiners, Cabal and a Kolo Muani penalty. The win came in Luciano Spalletti’s 600th Serie A game as a coach.

The Europa League comes first. Kick-off for Thursday’s league-phase meeting at the Allianz Stadium is at 21:00. Three days later they visit Como, one of the clubs above them, in round 13 on Sunday 29 November 2026 at 20:45.

The direct test against Inter is further away. The league meeting between the two clubs is set for Sunday 10 January 2027 at 20:45.

Markus Krösche is beginning to evaluate potential targets ahead of January, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s name is on his list.

Some movement is expected in the attacking department in the winter window, with Francesco Camarda potentially heading out on loan. According to Matteo Moretto (via Calciomercato.com), Kalimuendo’s name has come back into fashion as a potential replacement.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Milan had their eye on Kalimuendo several seasons ago, when the Frenchman moved from PSG to Rennes, where he truly exploded. Nothing came of it, partly because Nottingham Forest swooped in, signing him after a season with 18 goals and four assists in 34 games.

His adjustment to the Premier League didn’t go to plan, and last January he was loaned to Eintracht Frankfurt, where Krösche was working as the sporting director. The results were positive: six goals and one assist in 19 appearances.

Now the German will officially become Milan’s Head of Football, Kalimuendo could become a name to watch again. Forest could once again say yes to a loan, perhaps with a fixed option to buy as they did with Omari Hutchinson.

The 24-year-old is a versatile player who can operate either as a centre-forward or out wide, which is something that could well appeal to Ruben Amorim. This season he has played just 110 minutes for Forest spread across five appearances.

Endrick remains the priority, but if Real Madrid do not let him go, alternatives will be sought. The option of Santiago Gimenez returning to Milan from Porto, however, is not on the cards at the moment.

#1405. Benfica vs Famalicao - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 28 Nov 2026 17:12

Benfica will be looking to put their European disappointment behind them when they welcome Famalicao to Estadio da Luz on Monday evening.

The Eagles sit second in the Primeira Liga table with 28 points from 11 matches, five behind leaders Porto, while the 10th-placed visitors have collected 13 points from the same number of games and are five points above the relegation zone.

Benfica return to domestic action looking to respond after suffering a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Viktoria Plzen in the Europa League on Thursday, which ended their perfect start in the competition and halted a nine-game winning run in competitive outings.

That setback followed a 3-1 victory over second-tier Torreense in the Taca de Portugal, while the Eagles have also won each of their last four Primeira Liga matches, including a dramatic 3-2 success at Estrela Amadora in their most recent league outing, where Vangelis Pavlidis scored a stoppage-time winner.

Benfica have found the net a league-high 30 times while conceding 10 goals at the other end and have won nine of their 11 matches (W1, D1) in the top flight this season, although Porto's perfect record means there is little room for further mistakes in the title race.

With Porto facing a huge test against third-placed Sporting Lisbon a day earlier, the Eagles will be hoping for a favourable result in that encounter before turning their attention to securing all three points at home.

Indeed, Benfica have won 10 of their 11 matches at Estadio da Luz across all competitions this season, with the only blemish coming against newly promoted Academico on the opening day of the league campaign.

Famalicao, meanwhile, arrive under the permanent leadership of Ricardo Silva, who was confirmed as head coach on November 11 after initially taking charge on an interim basis following Carlos Carvalhal's departure.

The 46-year-old has overseen four matches since stepping up, recording two wins, one draw and one defeat, with his first outing producing an emphatic 4-0 victory away to Rio Ave before he guided the club into the Taca da Liga final four by eliminating Braga on penalties.

Although Famalicao subsequently suffered a 3-0 league defeat to the same opponents, Silva secured another victory in his most recent Primeira Liga outing, with Paulo Moreira scoring a 96th-minute winner in a 1-0 success over Arouca on November 6.

Returning to competitive action after a three-week break, Famalicao will be looking to build on that result and secure consecutive top-flight victories for the first time since winning three in a row between March 6 and 21.

The visitors have won three of their 11 league matches this season (D4, L4) and can take some encouragement from their away form, having collected eight of their 13 points on the road.

However, Famalicao must overcome a poor record at Estadio da Luz, having failed to win any of their previous 15 visits across all competitions, with their only top-flight point at the ground in that spell coming in a goalless draw during the 2021-22 campaign.

Benfica will be without Leandro Barreiro, who remains sidelined with a muscle injury, although club captain Fredrik Aursnes could return after making progress in his recovery from a thigh injury, although his availability remains uncertain.

Gianluca Prestianni is also likely to be available after missing Thursday's defeat through adductor fatigue and could feature on the flanks.

Pavlidis leads the early Golden Boot race with 11 Primeira Liga goals, two more than Sporting's Luis Suarez, and the Greek forward will be looking to add to his tally against Famalicao.

The visitors, meanwhile, could be without Matheus Mattara, who has not made the squad for any of their last three league outings, although Rodrigo Pinheiro is available again after serving his suspension.

Georgios Koutsias leads Famalicao's scoring charts with five league goals this season and is expected to lead the line at Da Luz.

Soares; Bah, Araujo, Lenglet, Dahl; Palhinha, Sudakov; Schjelderup, Echeverri, Prestianni; Pavlidis

Benfica will be eager to respond to their defeat in Plzen, and their strong domestic form, coupled with Famalicao's poor record at Estadio da Luz, makes the hosts favourites to secure a convincing victory.

#1404. Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and important for the win as well.'

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

#1403. Casa Pia vs Braga - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 28 Nov 2026 17:19

Casa Pia will be looking to end their miserable home record when they welcome Braga to Estadio Municipal de Rio Maior on Monday evening.

The hosts sit 16th in the Primeira Liga table with eight points from 11 matches, behind 15th-placed Maritimo on the head-to-head tiebreaker, while the eighth-placed Archbishops are three points adrift of Arouca in fifth.

Since replacing Carlos Vicens in October, Franclim Carvalho has overseen an impressive turnaround at Braga, placing greater emphasis on defensive organisation after taking charge of a side that had suffered three consecutive defeats.

The 39-year-old began his tenure with a 2-0 victory over Gent in the Conference League before experiencing consecutive setbacks, losing 1-0 away to Nacional in his first league match and then suffering a penalty shootout defeat to Famalicao in the Taca da Liga.

However, Braga have since won four of their last five matches (D1), keeping clean sheets in all five encounters and scoring 10 goals during that run, with their latest success coming in a 4-0 thrashing of KuPS in the Conference League on Thursday.

That European triumph, which lifted the Minho club to 10th in the 36-team table, followed a Taca de Portugal victory over Vitoria de Guimaraes and a 1-0 league success away to Rio Ave, having also beaten Famalicao in the Primeira Liga on November 1.

Looking to win three consecutive top-flight games for the first time since winning four in a row between January and mid-February, Braga must also improve an away record of two victories from six league trips this season (D2, L2), although their most recent outing on the road was that triumph at Vila dos Conde.

After securing their place in this season's top flight through the playoffs following a 16th-placed finish last term, Casa Pia have found themselves in familiar difficulties under Filipe Coelho, who succeeded Alvaro Pacheco earlier in the summer.

Much of their trouble has stemmed from an attack that has managed just six league goals this season, the second-fewest tally in the division, while conceding 20 at the other end to underline the need for improvement across the pitch.

Although the team appeared to have sparked a revival between September 20 and October 24, winning three of four matches across all competitions (L1) after failing to take maximum points from any of their opening six league fixtures, they have since gone three games without a victory.

Casa Pia's latest downturn began with a 2-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon before a 1-1 draw away to Alverca, while last weekend's 1-0 loss to second-tier Atletico CP saw Coelho's side eliminated from the Taca de Portugal in the fourth round.

A return to Rio Maior offers little encouragement for the hosts, who have lost all five matches at the ground this term by a combined score of 15-1, including a 7-0 mauling by Benfica on August 17.

If the head-to-head record offers any reason for optimism, Casa Pia will hope to draw inspiration from their double over Braga two seasons ago, although those victories account for their only successes in the last seven league meetings, with the other five ending in defeat.

Casa Pia remain without goalkeeper Andre Gomes, who is recovering from an injury and has only recently returned to partial training, leaving Ivan Mandic and Patrick Sequeira as the available options, with the latter having started each of the last three league matches.

Joao Rego is expected to return to the starting lineup after recovering from the physical issue that forced him to leave Portugal's Under-21 squad and miss the cup defeat to Atletico CP.

Jeremy Livolant made his first league start of the season against Alverca and could feature from the outset again, having made a substitute appearance in last weekend's cup loss.

Braga, meanwhile, will be without Vitor Carvalho after the midfielder sustained an injury during training ahead of Thursday's European fixture.

Sikou Niakate also remains sidelined with a long-term Achilles injury, while Jonas Wind has returned to group training and could be available after head coach Carvalho confirmed that the striker may be an option.

Club captain Ricardo Horta is expected to return to the starting lineup after being rested against KuPS, with Pau Victor and Fran Navarro also pushing to retain their places after both scored in that continental outing.

After largely being in the hands of one man for six years, AC Milan’s left wing has a new star shining: Alphadjo Cisse.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write how Cisse has hit 10 goals for the season in all competitions, with in the league and four in the Europa League. The Italian has already caught up with Rafael Leao’s total for the 2025-26 season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The numbers may not tell the whole story, but they hardly lie. With his goal in Athens, Cisse contributed to Milan’s incredible comeback against Olympiacos and reached double figures for the season, equaling Leao’s 10 goals in the entirety of last season before the end of November.

The most striking statistic is Cisse’s scoring rate: one goal every 78 minutes played, a sign of the 20-year-old’s ability to be ready whenever Ruben Amorim calls upon him, even during the game if necessary. Yet, Milan are enjoying the exploits of Cisse on the same flank, a young player who plays with a smile like Rafa did. The former Verona starlet always plays at a high tempo, attacks the space in behind with conviction, and finishes most of the chances that come his way.

Comparing Alpha to Leao’s first season shows how quickly he has adapted. In 2019-20 the Portuguese player managed six goals in 33 appearances across the league and the Coppa Italia. His scoring peak was 16 goals in 2022-23.

Cisse is already at 10 before December, and this has led to suggestions that a contract renewal could be forthcoming to fend off mounting interest in the Premier League.

#1401. No bans after matchday 12: Juventus and Como at full strength for the Sinigaglia

The Serie A disciplinary judge suspended no players after matchday 12, so neither Juventus nor Como lose anyone for Sunday's game. Como were fined again for a slow restart, and Juventus head to Lake Como five points behind them.

Juventus travel to Como on Sunday with no suspension worries. Nor do their hosts. Serie A disciplinary judge Gerardo Mastrandrea banned nobody after matchday 12 in a ruling published in Milan on 24 November.

The decisions covered the games of 21, 22 and 23 November. Nobody was sent off across the round. No player one booking from a ban picked up a yellow card either.

Juventus had no cards from their own fixture. The club’s match sheet for the 4-0 win over Venezia at the Allianz Stadium lists no bookings, with Arena as referee.

All four goals came after the break. Woltemade (53′), Koopmeiners (59′) and Cabal (65′) scored before Kolo Muani converted a penalty (71′).

Two Lecce players, Danilo Veiga and Jamil Siebert, picked up their fourth booking of the season and are now one caution from a ban, Virgilio Sport reported. No Juventus or Como player reached that threshold this round.

Como did not escape the judge entirely. The €8,000 fine was imposed under strict liability for delaying the start of the second half by about four minutes without good reason. The judge treated it as a repeated repeat offence.

It was the largest of the round’s penalties for late restarts. Fiorentina and Milan were also fined as repeat offenders. Genoa received €3,000 for a two-minute delay to kick-off.

The problem is not new for Como. In the previous round, the communiqué of 10 November fined them €10,000, again as repeated repeat offenders. On that occasion the second half started about two minutes late.

Juventus were not blameless that week. The same 10 November ruling fined them €5,000 for holding up the start of the first half by the same margin as Como’s latest delay.

The match carries weight in the race for the top four. Como have 8 wins, 2 draws and 2 defeats from their 12 games. They have scored 20 goals and conceded 10.

Juventus have 6 wins, 3 draws and 3 defeats. Their attack, with 19 goals, has almost kept pace with Como’s. The difference lies at the back, where Juventus have conceded 12.

A win on Lake Como would narrow the gap to their hosts. Defeat would push Juventus further from the top four.

Como host Juventus at the Sinigaglia on 29 November.

#1400. Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

“We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager said. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

United fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw

It had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and quickly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after big-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

All eyes are on this one. Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1399. Man United break another unwanted Premier League record in 4-0 Brentford defeat

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 17:48, Last updated: 28 Nov 2026 17:48

Manchester United suffered an all-time defensive worst in their embarrassing 4-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford at Old Trafford.

Red Devils fans may have trekked to Mauricio Pochettino's first home game with a renewed sense of optimism after an encouraging display in their 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon during the week.

Man United had control of the opening exchanges against Brentford, but they failed to make their dominance count and fell behind to Callum Wilson's strike in the 19th minute.

Wilson's opener preceded another rearguard catastrophe from the relegation-threatened Red Devils, as the veteran Englishman added a second before half time before Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade completed the rout.

Even before Ajer and Schade's goals put Brentford out of sight, Man United broke yet another unwanted record, becoming the first team to concede multiple goals in six straight halves of Premier League football.

The Red Devils had previously shipped 2+ goals in both halves against Liverpool and Aston Villa, while also letting in a pair in the second half of their 2-0 defeat to Chelsea.

Not since the first 45 minutes of their defeat at Stamford Bridge have Man United avoided conceding in a half of Premier League football, and Brentford's late double means that they have now shipped 2+ goals in seven consecutive Premier League halves.

Boos rang out at both half time and full time at an increasingly toxic Old Trafford, as Brentford rejoiced in their first league away victory over Man United since 1937, ending an 89-year barren spell.

Club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox were also targeted by furious Man United supporters, who bellowed out 'You're not to fit to wear the shirt' at demoralised players as they made their way off the field.

After 11 games of the 2025-26 Premier League season, Tottenham Hotspur had 18 points, and they only survived relegation on the final day of the campaign.

After 12 games of the 2026-27 season, Man United have eight points, are languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table and could plunge to 20th if Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday.

Together with the worst defence in Europe's big five leagues (40 goals conceded), Man United are undoubtedly sleepwalking towards a season in the Championship without a significant defensive restructuring.

Ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole that Man United must have relegation in the back of their minds, and today's evidence will only deepen fears of a first demotion in over 50 years.

#1398. THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:37 EST, 25 November 2026

After Florian Wirtz trudged off the field just over an hour into Liverpool’s defeat by Manchester City in October, sacrificed following Ryan Gravenberch’s red card, Jamie Carragher had once again seen enough of the £116million man.

‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ said Carragher post-match. ‘I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again.’

Fast forward six weeks, and Wirtz was running the show for Liverpool as they put four past Manchester United in poor Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, topping a stellar performance off with a goal and an assist. Carragher hailed the German’s stunning first-half volley as ‘a goal Dennis Bergkamp would have scored’.

How things change. This was a performance, even against an abysmal 10-man United, that showed Wirtz was ready, at last, to seize the big occasions.

Because, for so long, he wasn’t ready. Carragher was not alone in his earlier assessment, one shared by countless frustrated Liverpool fans. There was a feeling that this slight, wispy technician had the tools to flourish in the slower-paced Bundesliga, or even for Liverpool in the Champions League, but would, perhaps, remain unable to shine amid the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

Wirtz managed five goals and four assists in the Premier League last season and added only one assist this term before that City game. Since then, he’s come to life. Four assists and a couple of goals in the league with another one of each in the Champions League, a tally he will hope to add to on Wednesday evening against Club Bruges.

Florian Wirtz has suddenly sprung to life as a Liverpool player and is making his critics eat their words

Wirtz scores a majestic flick against Manchester United on Sunday

Since that City defeat, Wirtz is getting into dangerous positions more often. He is having more touches in the opposition box, more shots in the opposition box, playing more passes into the opposition box and creating more than twice as many chances from open play.

Wirtz boasts a league-high 29 of those this season, and 20 of the chances have come since that City game.

The last player to create more than the 10 open-play chances Wirtz managed against United was David Silva in 2015. Wirtz created nine against Brentford, too, in the first league match after the City defeat, meaning he’s the only Premier League player on record (since 2003-04) to create nine or more chances from open play in multiple games in the same season. Wirtz did it twice in five weeks.

Let’s nip this one in the bud early. It is clear, of course, that Jurgen Klopp, the legendary former Liverpool manager now Germany head coach, has got a tune out of Wirtz in recent months. The pair, according to those who follow the national team, are very close.

‘Wirtz is a once-in-a-century talent,’ was Klopp’s assessment last year, while he later remarked that he was ‘shocked’ by how good Wirtz was in their first training session together.

The 23-year-old has shown it in matches, too, with four goals and an assist in his last four games for Germany, including a brace last week against the Netherlands.

This has fed a narrative of how Klopp has been the one to unlock Wirtz’s powers. Klopp deserves credit, naturally, but he is also helped by having the freedom to give Wirtz what he needs: space.

‘What do I need to be at my best? Ideally, a lot of space in every game so I can do what I want!’ said Wirtz after scoring one and setting up the other in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia in October.

He was half-joking, laughing as he said it, but he’s right. Technical creators like Wirtz thrive on space. He’s been able to have more of that in international football, with Klopp even playing him as a false nine to give him all the creative freedom he needs. He leads the press but the midfielders behind him do the bulk of the dirty work to allow Wirtz, the star, to shine.

Wirtz’s performances with his country have helped grow his confidence, but it would be deeply unfair on Iraola to suggest Klopp’s blueprint is the one now being copied.

Even if Liverpool and Germany play a similar style, it is much, much harder to give players freedom in the Premier League.

But if anyone was going to find a way to do it for Wirtz, it was Iraola.

Arne Slot could never work it out. By the end of his tenure, he’d played Wirtz as an attacking midfielder, stuck him on both flanks and thrust him up front. It was a conundrum he just couldn’t solve.

Iraola's Bournemouth side were one of the hardest-working, highest-pressing teams in the division but his system was still able to allow the likes of Justin Kluivert or Junior Kroupi to create and drift into pockets of space to set the attacking tempo.

For Iraola, it was always going to be Wirtz. The German has started every league game, all of them in the No 10 position.

He’s always led the way off the ball – only three players have won possession more often in the final third this season – but Iraola has been finding different ways to get the best out of him with the ball, too. Against Brentford, he shifted Rio Ngumoha inside almost to play as a second No 10 beside Wirtz, which helped create space for him to set up Liverpool's equaliser.

Having Alexis Mac Allister behind him allows Wirtz to concentrate on being the creative heartbeat, while even Dominik Szoboszlai has played noticeably deeper since returning from injury.

Andoni Iraola has started Wirtz in every league game, all of them in the No 10 position

Szoboszlai isn't the only one. Another aspect of Germany's game that has helped Wirtz is lining up alongside strikers who like to drop deep in Kai Havertz and Nick Woltemade, leaving space for Wirtz to attack.

In recent weeks, especially against United, Liverpool striker Alexander Isak has been doing the same. It was Isak doing exactly that which led to Wirtz’s goal.

Isak (below, in possession) drops in, plays the ball out wide to Ngumoha and Wirtz sprints into the box to get on to the end of the cross.

Alexander Isak dropped into midfield and sprayed the ball wide to Rio Ngumoha before Wirtz's goal against United

Isak missed much of last season through injury but his all-round play is much better attuned to Wirtz's game than those who played alongside him for most of 2025-26, including Hugo Ekitike.

One of the most devastating aspects of Iraola’s Bournemouth was how quickly players flooded forward when they attacked.

His Liverpool side is starting to do the same which, in turn, helps get the best out of Wirtz.

Last season under Slot, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Mo Salah would often tuck in instead of bombing forward out wide and Milos Kerkez, one of the most attacking full backs in the division under Iraola at Bournemouth, rarely did the same under Slot.

Now, Liverpool’s wingers are flying. This season under Iraola, Liverpool are averaging more ‘fast breaks’, how Opta define counter attacks, and shots from them than in any campaign under Slot or even the ‘heavy metal’ Klopp.

Wirtz has attempted seven through balls this season, one of the highest tallies in the division. Since the City game in particular, he has tried to play passes with purpose into the box.

Wirtz was creating chances in the first six games of this season but only a few of them were penetrating passes into the box

The German's chances created in the last five games, since the City defeat, show how many balls he is playing into dangerous areas

The rapid Bradley Barcola starting to find his feet since his £123m move has been a huge help to Wirtz.

Of Wirtz’s 20 open-play chances created since the City game, a quarter of them have been for Barcola.

Having those runners out wide like Barcola and Ngumoha is so helpful for the German. As he drives forward with the ball against United (below), he has three runners ahead of him with even Szoboszlai bursting forward. Wirtz has so many options and eventually slips in Isak for a great chance.

Liverpool had wide runners driving forward against United, helping Wirtz create chances and split their defence

You can see from the average position map from the game (below), just how attacking Liverpool’s wingers – and Kerkez – were, albeit, granted, against 10 men for most of the contest.

The average position map of Liverpool's players against United shows how high up the pitch they played

Wirtz has had a run like this before, around this time last year. During December and January, he racked up four league goals and three assists – having not managed a single one until then – only to notch one of each for the rest of the Premier League campaign.

You get the sense, though, with his confidence growing under managers for both club and country who want to play his way, that he might just keep shining this time.

Musah was born in the USA, but his parents moved almost immediately after to Italy where he lived until age 9, when they moved to England. He was in the Arsenal academy when the England youth teams first called him up, and he was in the England U15, U17, and U19 teams. At age 16, he chose to leave the Arsenal system for Valencia. It was while he was with Valencia that a coach working for the US Soccer Federation who had been in charge of the Valencia youth system heard about him and his eligibility to play for the US, and so he was contacted and accepted a callup to play in some friendlies with the senior USMNT team at age 17 (going on 18) in 2020. Italy could have tried to recruit him also, but never once contacted him. Without this aggressive outreach to international players with multiple nationalities, the USMNT would be a much, much weaker team.

#1396. Locatelli tells young Juventus fans he has learned to accept long knee layoff

Juventus captain Manuel Locatelli has called his knee injury one of the hardest spells of his career. Answering questions from young members of the club, he said his recovery is on track and that he has learned to live with a long wait.

Manuel Locatelli has not played since early September, and the Juventus captain admits the time away has been tough. Speaking in a new episode of the club’s Junior Reporter series, in which children from the Juventus membership programme interview a first team player, the midfielder was open about how he is coping.

As ANSA reported on Tuesday evening, Locatelli put the injury alongside Italy’s failure to reach the World Cup as the lowest points of his time as a professional.

Locatelli explained that he hurt his knee and now has to stay off the pitch for a long time. He said he feels good and that the work is going well, much of it in the gym rather than on the grass.

“I miss playing football so much, so much, but I have learned to accept this situation,” he told the young reporters, according to the quotes carried by Calciomercato.com. He added that he knows he has to give it time, and that he must do his best to come back in good shape.

On the national team, he did not hide the pain of missing out on the tournament. “When you lose, and lose like that, it is a moment of suffering,” he said.

The problem dates back to 6 September, when Locatelli sprained his right knee in the 1-1 home draw against Milan. Two days later Juventus confirmed in an official medical update that he had undergone surgery in Lyon to suture the external meniscus. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the operation with club doctor Marco Freschi in attendance, and rehabilitation started the following day.

The club gave no return date at the time. ANSA now says the captain expects to be available again in the first months of 2027, while Football Italia reports that he is not expected back in full training before March.

Locatelli also spoke about leadership. He said becoming captain was an ambition he had from the moment he arrived from Sassuolo in 2021, and he credited Giorgio Chiellini, Leonardo Bonucci and Danilo for showing him what it means to be present for the group every day. His childhood idols, he said, were Pavel Nedved, Gianluigi Buffon, Alessandro Del Piero and Francesco Totti.

The club tied him down in April, when he signed a new contract until June 2030.

His absence has forced Luciano Spalletti to reshape his midfield for most of the autumn, a problem we looked at when Thuram and Locatelli were both missing earlier this month.

Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday on the back of a 4-0 win over Venezia, and go to Como on Sunday with a clean bill on the disciplinary front, as covered in our piece on the matchday 12 rulings. Their captain, for now, remains a spectator, but by his own account a patient one.

#1393. Como beat AEK with eight players missing, then faded late before hosting Juventus

Como beat AEK Athens 1-0 to reach 12 points in the Champions League, despite eight unavailable players and a late drop in intensity. Juventus visit the Sinigaglia on Sunday, but must first play Omonia on Thursday.

The narrow victory over AEK was Como’s third straight win in the Champions League. It leaves them close to the knockout stage. It also offers the latest look at Juventus’s next league opponents, on the same ground.

The win came with a stretched squad. Fàbregas told Sky Sport that the absentees were either injured or left out of the Champions League squad list. Making so few changes was, he said, a first in his coaching career. That is a thin bench ahead of a league weekend.

The scoreline flattered AEK in places. Lucas Da Cunha missed a first-half penalty, and Nico Paz hit the post. At the other end, goalkeeper Robert Sánchez made two important saves before the break. Milla’s goal made him the 11th different player to score for Como in this season’s competition. No other team in the Champions League has had that many different scorers. UEFA named him Player of the Match.

Como had been scoring freely before Matchday 5. On Matchday 4 they won 9-1 away to Lens, a result that put them fourth at the halfway point of the league phase. AEK proved a harder problem. They held Como up for long spells and were difficult to break down.

The final stretch was the concern. Fabio Capello put it to Fàbregas that Como had dropped off badly in the last 20 minutes. The coach replied that he did not yet have the experience to stay calm in such moments. The late fade is consistent with a group short on fresh legs.

Fàbregas also set out his priorities. He said the win brought Como close to at least a play-off place, but that qualification was not yet secured. In the same breath, he stressed that Serie A matters more to the club. That message points straight at Sunday’s meeting with Juventus.

Juventus have their own European commitment first. Kick-off in Turin, in the Europa League league phase, is at 20:00 UTC. Juve go into that game fifth with 10 points from four matches. Omonia are 18th with six. Sam Barrott of England will referee, with Darren England on VAR.

That schedule cuts into any advantage from Como’s fatigue. Both sides will carry European minutes into the weekend. Juve, however, will have had two fewer days to recover.

The league table adds weight to the fixture. Como sit fourth in Serie A, eight points ahead of Juventus. A home defeat would leave a depleted Como squad with a reduced cushion. A Juve win would close the gap at the end of a demanding week.

Como’s Champions League campaign continues away to Real Betis on 9 December, and the league phase ends with a trip to Barcelona on Wednesday 27 January 2027. After Sunday’s 13th-round meeting at the Sinigaglia, Juventus host Udinese at 18:00 on Sunday 6 December.

#1390. Man Utd 0-4 Brentford: Red Devils match shocking 63-year feat but promising stat emerges

By Ben Knapton | 28 Nov 2026 18:08

Manchester United equalled an appalling 63-year feat in their 4-0 Premier League defeat to Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Mauricio Pochettino's first home game in charge of the Red Devils was nothing short of a horror show, as the Bees won a league game away to their hosts for the first time since 1937.

Despite a bright start from Man United, they were unable to convert their early promise into a goal and fell behind just before the 20-minute mark through Callum Wilson.

The former West Ham United and Newcastle United striker then doubled his tally for the afternoon before the break, seeing Man Utd become the first team in Premier League history to concede 2+ goals in six straight halves.

A shocking six became a sorry seven in the second period, when Kristoffer Ajer and Kevin Schade completed the humiliation on a day when Man United broke another unwanted Premier League record.

? 12 games, 1 win for Manchester United in Premier League this season. ? 10 games in a row without a win. ?❌ https://t.co/SyI1S2SoSG

As well as finding themselves on the wrong side of league history - again - the current Man United crop suffered yet another club worst in the Premier League era.

Today's result marked the first time in the competition that Man United had lost back-to-back fixtures by 4+ goals, after also going down 4-0 to bitter rivals Liverpool last weekend.

The last time Man United suffered two four-goal league defeats in a row was back in December 1963, when they were thrashed 4-0 by Everton and then 6-1 by Burnley on Boxing Day.

Matt Busby's men ended up finishing in second place in the First Division that year, but this time around, Man United are now second from bottom in the Premier League table with just eight points from 12 fixtures.

The Red Devils' winless run in the top flight now stands at a terrible 10 matches, and they will drop to 20th place on Sunday if Crystal Palace - who are one point behind with a worse goal difference - beat Hull City.

To say that little has gone Pochettino's way since he joined Man Utd would be an understatement, as the Argentine was firstly hamstrung by costly and inexplicable refereeing decisions against Liverpool and Sporting Lisbon.

Pochettino then presided over an excellent first 20-or-so minutes against Brentford, but in the absence of Benjamin Sesko - and with Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha on the bench - they lacked a killer touch to convert their opportunities.

The Red Devils nevertheless generated more Expected Goals than the Bees - 2.39 to 2.30 - offering a tiny glimmer of hope for the months ahead under Pochettino.

However, for as long as Man United's defence remains as porous as it is - now 40 goals conceded across all tournaments this season - no amount of attacking endeavour can save the Red Devils from a relegation scrap.

More than nine years on, the Brazilian is in line to start again in black and white, with first choice Guglielmo Vicario being rested for the visit of the Cypriot side to the Allianz Stadium.

His most recent competitive outing came on 30 May with Botafogo, as Football Italia noted after Wednesday’s press conference. Since then he has been working as cover, a role he took on after joining as a free agent at the end of September.

Juventus moved for Neto after Kamil Grabara ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in training on 19 September, only days after keeping a clean sheet on his debut against NEC. The club confirmed his return on 28 September with a contract running until 30 June 2027.

Asked what drew him back, Neto explained that he had been looking for a next step that genuinely meant something to him. “Deep down, I felt my chapter with Juve was still open,” he said, in comments reported by ilBianconero, which carried the press conference live. He added that he is enjoying his work and is in Turin to help, whatever the coming months bring.

Opening the press conference, he described his feelings simply: “It’s hugely satisfying. I’m really excited to be back on the pitch, and proud to be part of this team.”

Neto was asked about Vicario, who is on loan from Tottenham and has been Luciano Spalletti’s regular choice in goal. He kept his answer short: “I don’t know how much my opinion matters, but he’s a top-level goalkeeper.”

The veteran also spoke warmly about the younger players around him. He said their eagerness to contribute was infectious and that the squad has the quality, will and determination it needs. On the goals Juventus have conceded this season, he pointed to a side that is still developing, with several players new to Serie A and finding their way. His own focus, he said, is on training at full intensity every day while the team looks for balance and consistency.

Juventus go into matchday five fifth in the league phase standings with ten points from four games. Omonia have won two and lost two. Neto warned against taking them lightly, saying they are a strong side who break forward with real quality, and revealed he knows Omonia’s Fabiano from his years in Brazil.

He also stressed that Europe brings its own demands, noting that Juventus always carry a responsibility to compete to win in every tournament they enter.

Interest in the meeting was already strong after ticket sales for Omonia passed 35,000 last week. Next up in Serie A is the trip to Como, where both sides go in without suspensions.

For Neto, the night is a chance to add to the 22 appearances he made in his first spell, when he won two league titles, two Coppa Italia trophies and a Supercoppa Italiana as Gianluigi Buffon’s understudy.
