#1261. Torreense 1-2 Celtic: Camilo Duran springs from the bench to get Bhoys out of jail again

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:40 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 18:11 EST, 26 November 2026

Some 90 miles north of the scene of the club’s crowning moment, Celtic ensured that their latest return to Portugal did not tarnish the legacy of the Lisbon Lions.

Sleep would not have come easily to Martin O’Neill ahead of this awkward assignment in the small city of Leiria.

Almost 60 years ago, the Northern Irishman watched Jock Stein’s legendary side defeat Inter Milan on a black-and-white television while in boarding school.

For the current side to fail to see off a second division side in Torreense would have been embarrassing enough at the best of times. For it to have happened in this season of all seasons would have added to the sense of shame.

In a game where a victory was really the only acceptable outcome, O’Neill’s men toiled for the longest time yet got there in the end.

Yet again, Camilo Duran was the toast of the visiting supporters as he claimed his 15th goal of the season with six minutes remaining.

Celtic's performance certainly wasn’t pretty. But after a diabolical start to this Europa League campaign, the Parkhead men are back in the saddle.

Camilo Duran celebrates after his 84th minute header saved Celtic's skins in Portugal

Now with back-to-back victories against Besiktas and Torreense, O’Neill’s men have more than a puncher’s chance of reaching the play-off round again.

One win from their remaining games with Omonia, Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise might get them there. Four points certainly will. It goes without saying, however, that they will have to produce much better than they did here.

After a tough six-week spell when the team looked lost, though, O’Neill has taken it to a better place. For just the third time this season, Celtic have chalked up four straight wins.

Although O’Neill had stressed that he still wanted to make an appreciable impact on Europe, there was an air of compromise about his line-up ahead of Sunday’s trip to Tynecastle.

Duran was initially stationed on the bench with Kasper Hogh, no goals in his past 16 games, tasked with leading the line. It’s fair to say the Dane did not enhance his reputation.

With Cameron Carter-Vickers nursing a strain, Dane Murray was stripped although the pair were swapped at the interval.

Jota, unsurprisingly, started in his homeland after being drafted into the squad as a replacement for the injured Mika Baur. By some distance, the winger was Celtic’s best player on the night.

The Colombian heads the ball home after a superb cross by fellow sub James Forrest

Built for Euro 2004, the Estadio Dr Magalhaes Pessoa in Leiria made for a strange backdrop to a match of such significance.

With Torreense forced by UEFA to play 60 miles from their own tiny ground, Celtic supporters outnumbered the Portuguese fans by two-to-one.

The fast start would have met with O’Neill’s approval. Liam Scales flicked on a corner which Adriel, Torreense’s Brazilian keeper, flapped at. Yang Hyun-jun’s goal-bound shot was blocked.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain then played a measured pass down the left to release Jota. The cross was attacked by Yang, but knocked clear. Amid the chaos, Hogh took a boot to the head which required treatment.

Jota was already relishing the task of tormenting Jonathan Mutombo. When he faced the right-back up on nine minutes, he eased past him in a blur of skill and pace.

The cross which followed was menacing. Stood at the far post, Javi Vazquez, under pressure from Yang, tried to usher the ball round the post and got it all wrong. He lashed the ball into his own net. Celtic had the early breakthrough they craved so badly.

It's relief for Martin O'Neill after Duran sprung from the bench to seal a 2-1 victory

With Torreense then compelled to come out, everything was in Celtic’s favour. Provided they maintained the tempo of the match and their quality on the ball, it had the makings of a comfortable night. So much for that theory.

For reasons only they could explain, Celtic became sloppy with the ball and lethargic without it.

Torreense served a warning that the game wasn’t done when Sam Johnstone had to boot away a free-kick. It wasn’t heeded.

Arriving on 19 minutes, the nature of the leveller was shocking from O’Neill’s perspective. Alex Alfaro was given far too much time on the edge of the box to take aim and fire. The ball bounced back off the bar.

Kieran Tierney panicked and sliced a clearance. As Dany Jean pounced, Colby Donovan put in a half-hearted tackle. The Haiti international smashed the ball home from an angle.

Could Celtic quickly respond? Not if they were depending on Hogh. The Dane earned a break of the ball and couldn’t pick out Jota.

Hogh’s ball retention started to go from bad to worse. Yang, who’d begun the game brightly, was equally as culpable of that failing.

Time and again Celtic looked to Jota to provide a moment of magic. He danced away from Manu Pozo on the flank and fired a rocket towards goal. Adriel beat it away.

Another terrific delivery from the winger presented Hogh with another chance to end his goal drought. Again, he lacked any conviction and the keeper made a routine save.

Camilo Duran goes over to celebrate in front of the fans who made the trip to Portugal

Torreense were not without their moments. Scales was forced to clear the ball off the line after Volnei Feltes had enjoyed a free header following a foul.

Hogh did well to pick the pocket of Stopira in the right channel. The Cape Verde international breathed a sigh of relief as the forward again failed to steer the ball away from Adriel’s arms as a raft of visiting players were poised to claim a tap-in.

Another excellent delivery from Jota saw Luke McCowan win the ball at the back post. On this occasion, it was hard to fault Hogh for not connecting with the headed ball back across goal.

The second half simply had to be much better from Celtic. Jota was gifted a chance to claim a second when Stopira passed the ball straight to him. His chip didn’t have quite enough to beat the keeper.

Jota dribbled his way to the line and centred. Oxlade-Chamberlain let the ball run to Tierney. The full-back lashed a shot which Feltes stood up tall to block.

Donovan’s weak strike was the cue for O’Neill to ring the changes, with Duran and Oliver Sorensen replacing Hogh and Oxlade-Chamberlain.

Before either substitute had enjoyed a touch of the ball, the impressive Jean fired into Johnstone’s side-net. This was not going to plan.

Duran is hailed by team-mates Donovan and Forrest after his late rescue act for Celtic

O’Neill’s men were mighty fortunate not to fall behind with 20 minutes left. Scales completely misjudged a long ball. Carter-Vickers didn’t provide cover. Musa Drammeh, the former Hearts forward, ought to have done better to fire his shot beyond the far post.

With Jota off after tiring, it all got rather desperate. Within the space of 60 seconds, Yang let a simple pass roll under his foot before Sorensen ran the ball out of play.

It was to be a combination of an old stager and the man of the moment which saved the day, however.

With six minutes remaining, substitute James Forrest bobbed and weaved his way down the right and sent in a cross which you’d seen a thousand times. Duran attacked it and thumped home a clinical header.

Played in by Forrest, McCowan was prevented from claiming a late third by the keeper’s legs. Relief was the overriding emotion at the end.

#1259. Thomas Frank earns his first Crystal Palace victory as boss, Bournemouth win TENTH game in a row with comeback, and Brighton thrash Romanian minnows - but Sunderland are held at home

By LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER and BEN WINSTANLEY and WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER and MILES STARFORTH

Published: 15:09 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EST, 26 November 2026

Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.

But when Chris Richards' long-throw made its way to Jean-Philippe Mateta, everything changed on a chaotic night at Selhurst Park.

The French forward was pulled down by Jon Martin, who was sent off, and after Mateta tucked away his penalty, a flat performance and atmosphere was transformed.

Having been dominated, Palace were now quick, confident and incisive, and it was the Basque outfit who were on the ropes as Daichi Kamada saw an effort cleared off the line.

Jorgen Strand Larsen then attempted an audacious bicycle kick which fell to the feet of Dwight McNeil yards out to send the home fans into delirium.

It could have been more, but Yeremy Pino's penalty in added time was saved and Strand Larsen missed an open goal. Dean Henderson then made a brilliant stop to secure the three points.

Thomas Frank got his first win as Crystal Palace boss as his side came from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1

Palace's season has been a disaster thus far, but it now has lift-off, and most importantly belief, heading into Sunday's crunch clash with Hull.

'It could be (a turning point) but we need to follow it up with a good performance against Hull,' said Frank. 'But you can take a lot of positives. What I really liked is the belief from the players and that we were a threat on set pieces.

'The penalty and red card changed the game. It’s not easy 10 vs 11, but we were brave and it paid off - and then we were all close to a heart attack in the last five minutes!'

Frank, who received a warm reception from the Eagles faithful ahead of his first home game, handed rare starts to Will Hughes, Ben Chilwell and Eddie Nketiah as he rang the changes after last week’s defeat by Coventry.

They practised defending set-pieces in the warm-up in an attempt to deal with what has become their kryptonite, yet Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr almost turned in at the far post from a free kick just minutes in.

After a poor opening half hour, Sociedad stepped things up and Henderson was forced into a string of good saves. Palace’s midfield was struggling and the Basque outfit should have gone ahead when Mikel Oyarzabal somehow fired straight at Henderson from a few yards out.

The England keeper had to be alert again soon after, yet the pressure paid off when Sarr turned home from Job Ochieng's cross.

But the game changed with Mateta's intervention, before McNeil ensured that, despite the injury-time mayhem, Frank is more than happy to be back in the madhouse of management.

'The feeling after a win on the pitch with players, staff and fans, but also in the changing room is so difficult to describe - it’s so unique,' said Frank. 'You like to experience a lot of that, but the hectic last 15 minutes, that was crazy.'

'The red card and penalty were the decisive action in the match,' added Sociedad boss Pellegrino Matarazzo. 'We controlled the match completely up until that. We tried to stabilise, but we could not hold them off long enough.'

Can anybody stop Bournemouth? For long stretches here it looked as if their relentless march would finally be stopped - but the 10-man Cherries found another gear to continue their rampage.

Marco Rose’s men have won 10 games in a row now, extending a club record. For two months, they have steamrolled their opponents with dauntless football and racked up an aggregate score of 25-3. They sit top of the Europa League with a perfect record.

Underneath the red and black armour, fans are starting to wonder if these players are actually of our species. Is Justin Kluivert a man or a cyborg? If you prick James Hill, does he bleed?

With each victory, the cry of the football world grows louder: somebody, please, stop this Bournemouth juggernaut, for the sake of everybody else’s trophy prospects.

Celta Vigo stepped up as the next challengers and thought they would be the heroes. They found Bournemouth’s net four times in all, but were denied by the offside flag for three of them. For long stretches, they were in command.

Bournemouth have now won 10 games in a row after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1

After a disappointing first half, Alvaro Rodriguez got them level early in the second

Rayan scored the winner against the run of play as Bournemouth continued their perfect run in the Europa League

In the first half, Bournemouth looked average. They were gifting away the ball in their own half, Celta found ways to sneak through their pincer-movement press, and the Spaniards had the better chances.

The first red flag came 11 minutes in, when Michele Di Gregorio spilled a save into the path of Pablo Duran, who dinked over the goalkeeper but saw his effort ruled out for offside.

Such warning bells were unheeded. Not long later, former Liverpool man Iago Aspas forced a save with a spectacular overhead kick at the age of 39.

Bournemouth failed to clear their lines, and Aspas punished the visitors, ghosting past Alex Scott on his return from injury before blasting beyond Di Gregorio with his left foot.

Things went from bad to worse minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a stamp on Couhaib Driouech, his yellow card upgraded to a red after a review by referee Harm Osmers.

Celta almost doubled their lead when Duran beat Di Gregorio again, but he had strayed offside.

The cameras panned to Rose, who stood looking bewildered on the sidelines, hands on hips. It took them 37 minutes for Kluivert to register their first shot. Bournemouth had been played off the park. This was a case of clinging on.

But the side that emerged in the second half were unrecognisable. If Bournemouth were a man down, they played with all the swagger of having an extra body.

They were level within two minutes of the restart, Alvaro Rodriguez glancing in from Amine Adli’s header.

Suddenly Bournemouth were their efflorescent selves again. Antonio Silva, Adli, and Rodriguez combined for a beautiful passage of play but were spurned by the offside flag. Hill tested Ionut Radu from range.

They finally got their rewards on the counter-attack, when Marcus Tavernier teed up his fellow substitute Rayan to slot past Radu and stun their hosts. Another comeback job complete.

And so the Bournemouth army marches on unfettered. In the next nine days, they face Fulham, Brighton, and Hull in the Premier League. By the time they visit Arsenal in mid-December, they may be breathing down their necks.

Earlier this week, Brighton CEO Paul Barber revealed the lengths that his club go to before agreeing to sign a player.

'We try and talk to people that know them, people that have coached them, people that played with them, sponsors that have worked with them, media that have interviewed them, maybe even neighbours that have lived next door to them,' he told Men in Blazers media network. 'You know, what sort of people are we talking about? Are we talking about players that are entirely focused on their work?'

There can be little doubt that the rigorous selection process is working, and two of their budget buys were on the scoresheet in the first half as they made light work of the Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova - and continued to make a mockery of the supposed challenge of balancing domestic and European assaults.

In the third minute Ibrahim Osman - £16.6m from Nordsjaelland in 2024 – finished off a sharp team move from close range after a pinpoint Jack Hinshelwood cross. Then shortly after the half-hour mark full back Maxime de Cuyper, £17m from Club Brugge in 2025, seized on a slack defensive ball into midfield, took two touches in advancing forward and - still well outside the box – wrongfooted the goalkeeper as he stroked the ball into the far corner. He made the finish look much easier than it was.

Brighton thrashed Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova and look capable of competing on multiple fronts

If the result was still in any doubt then, it wasn’t by the 39th minute when Vladimir Screciu was sent off for a clumsy challenge on Matt O’Riley. Referee Matthias Jollenbeck showed a yellow card but a replay showed a hefty tread on the ankle and - after being sent to his monitor - upgraded it to red.

The second half, then, gave the Seagulls a chance to remind everyone of their ruthless side. Already the highest scorers in the Premier League - averaging 2.4 per game this season – they wasted little time adding to their tally.

First, 19-year-old Charalampos Kostoulas made it three with his sixth of the season thanks to a cool finish on the hour mark, two minutes before Osman – like Hinshelwood a constant menace - picked the ball up on the left and cut inside to roll home his second.

They ended 90 minutes of domination having had 27 shots – one of which saw Femi Azeez missing the chance to make it five on debut by inexplicably blazing over from five yards.

Brighton have now scored four or more in five of their eight home games this season, and ended last night’s rout top of the Conference League having yet to concede a goal. The competition does not look big enough for them.

Sunderland still have work to do if the club is to reach the Europa League’s knockout stages after Jagiellonia Bialystok held them to a 1-1 draw in a game which saw some supporters of the Polish club evade a UEFA ban and get into the Stadium of Light.

Timur Tutierov’s second-half opener for Sunderland, hoping to secure a top-eight finish in the competition’s league phase and avoid the play-offs in their first European campaign in 53 years, was quickly cancelled out by the visitors.

‘It’s clear we are making many unforced errors this season leading to goals,’ said head coach Regis Le Bris. ‘The last two games, it didn’t happen, which is good, and now this is a reminder you can’t relax.’

Jagiellonia supporters had been banned from the game following crowd disturbances at the club’s fixture away to Levski Sofia on November 5.

But a number of visiting fans were removed from the stadium by police during the first half, and a “disappointed” Sunderland issued a statement after the game which claimed that Jagiellonia had “failed to engage and cooperate” with efforts to stop their supporters getting into home sections.

Le Bris had gone into the game without injured captain Granit Xhaka and striker Brian Brobbey, two of his most influential players. Sunderland’s head coach, mindful of forthcoming Premier League games against Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Newcastle United, took no chances with the pair for the visit of Jagiellonia, ninth in the Polish league.

Sunderland had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok

He made six changes from the team which had held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at the weekend, again fielding a youthful team in the competition.

A flat performance from a much-changed team had seen Sunderland beaten 2-0 by Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb in their last European outing at the Stadium of Light. The visiting section had been bouncing that night, in contrast to the empty seats for the visit of Jagiellonia.

On Wearside, the feeling ahead of the match was that third-bottom Sunderland, while shot shy, were slowly turning a corner, having taken four points from fixtures against Chelsea and Villa without conceding a goal to climb above Manchester United in the table.

The big one in Europe - AC Milan at the San Siro - is next in the competition for Sunderland, with the fixture having captured the imagination of supporters.

There were scarves with the slogan ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan? You’re about to!’ on sale outside the ground, with the merchandise a nod to a song which fans of their rivals Newcastle United can no longer sing.

Sunderland had an early scare when a Nik Prelec shot took a deflection off Ndah Sidiki, but Robin Roefs was able to gather the ball.

Within minutes of the game starting, it became apparent that a group of Polish fans had managed to buy tickets in the North Stand, and police were quickly called to remove them from the stadium amid cheers from Sunderland supporters.

On the pitch, it was another slow start for Le Bris’ side, though Malick Fofana tested Slawomir Abramowicz with a fine left-footed shot from outside the box.

Timur Tutierov was on target fo the Black Cats, but this was a flat performance

Enzo Le Fee did well to seize on a back pass in the 30th minute and cross from the left for Nilson Angulo - who was unmarked in the box - after rounding the goalkeeper. However, his shot struck the feet of Yuki Kobayashi.

Omar Alderete was forced off as the half-time break approached, and Roefs beat away a free-kick from Kajetan Szmyt.

Sunderland went into the break knowing they should have led, but their finishing had again let them down in the absence of Brobbey, their talisman.

Le Bris’ team were ahead within seconds of the restart. Rigg broke through the middle, and the ball was worked to Le Fee, whose cross bounced off a visiting defender on its way to Tutierov at the far post, who headed home.

The lead did not last, with Kamil Jozwiak seizing on a Nilson Reinildo backpass before rounding Roefs to level.

Roefs denied Jozwiak at the hour-mark with a low save as home fans became increasingly frustrated with their team.

A frustrated Le Bris said: ‘It’s hard to take, because we would like to have better football, better expression.’

#1258. Care Leavers Tour Hill Dickinson Stadium

Hill Dickinson Stadium welcomed some of Liverpool’s care experienced young people for an exclusive behind-the-scenes tour to mark National Care Leavers Month.

A group of 25 care leavers, who have either left or are preparing to leave local authority care, were given the opportunity to explore the Club’s stunning waterfront home.

Observed every November, National Care Leavers Month is a UK-wide campaign that celebrates care experienced young people, amplifies their voices and promotes positive change in policy and practice.

The youngsters, many of whom were visiting a football stadium for the first time, enjoyed an informative tour of the state-of-the-art venue, including the impressive home dressing room, the Media Centre, pitchside areas and learning about the heritage of the historic site.

Jenny Glennard, Corporate Director of Children & Young People’s Services at Liverpool City Council, said: "On behalf of Liverpool Children's Social Care, I would like to again extend my gratitude to Everton for providing our care experienced young people with the fantastic opportunity to visit Hill Dickinson Stadium as part of National Care Leavers Month.

"To be given a personal group tour was an experience and memory they will never forget. All of our young people have expressed how much they enjoyed the day and how impressed they were with the stadium, as well as the staff who made them feel so welcome.

"We value our relationship with Everton and look forward to continuing to work with the Club in the future."

Liverpool City Council's Leaving Care Services provide a wide range of support for young people transitioning from local authority care.

Using a person-centred approach to independent living skills, planning and assessment, the service aims to improve outcomes across education, training, employment, health and accommodation.

#1257. Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

#1256. Pollock at heart of scuffle that inspires Leicester to thumping win in feisty derby

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

The England back row, never knowingly far from controversy, escalated a brawl at the end of the first half that Leicester prop Joe Heyes revealed “added fuel to the fire” of a Tigers side who roared impressively when they returned after the break.

The incident fired up a sell-out crowd and Leicester brought what had up to that point been a drab game to life with a storming second-half performance.

Three tries in a pulverising 13-minute spell overturned a half-time deficit and put the hosts on course for a bonus-point win over their arch-rivals that took them to second place in the Prem table.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, said.

“We got on the front foot and showed our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we showed in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”

It was a chastening afternoon for the champions who last won at Welford Road in January 2023.

Phil Dowson, Saints’ director of rugby, felt his side were in the contest at the interval but bemoaned the fact that they were unable to handle Leicester’s second-half power surge.

“It was a scrap. The conditions were going to dictate that. And they had some set-piece dominance which hurt us,” he said.

“That gave them a ton of energy and we didn’t seem able to respond, which was probably the most disappointing thing.

“In the second half we didn’t seem to have that same buzz about us.”

Dowson was reluctant to blame the tunnel flare-up for the turnaround.

“It’s not as if anyone got filled in. Well, you just can’t anymore, can you? These games are going to be hostile and in the current game you can’t throw anything. It’s just push and shove and talk c--p, so I don’t think that had any impact.”

Northampton stand-off Fin Smith was withdrawn late on with a dead leg but he is expected to join up with the England squad for training on Monday.

Leicester Tigers: F Steward (G Pearson 79); A Radwan, W Wand (O Bailey 72), S Kata, G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet (T Whiteley 73); A van der Flier (T Haffar 73), J Blamire, (R Asiata 79), J Heyes (W Hurd 73), C Henderson (J Thompson 79), O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell (J Moro 72).

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith (O Sleightholme 72) A Mitchell (A McParland 58); E Iyogun (D Fischetti 62 ), C Langdon (R Smith 62), C Kundiona (I Neculai 51), A Coles, E Prowse, (JJ Van Der Mescht 62), J Kemeny, T Pearson (T Lockett 62), H Pollock (C Chick 52). Yellow card Lockett 70

That brings our coverage of today’s East Midlands derby to a close. Neil Squires’ full report will drop above soon. Thanks for joining us!

Leicester’s tight-head prop, who was named the player of the match, on those emotions at the break:

“It was a pretty hot changing room. We had to calm ourselves down a bit. But yeah, it added a bit of fuel to the fire. It means a lot to the locality. These fixtures are awesome and this is the best derby in the country.

“It’s part of the game isn’t it? Emotions are high, it’s physical. Everything’s in your face and there was a moment just before.

“We were frustrated in the first half. We had the ball in good areas. We went in and said let’s keep it simple, stick to the aerial contest and it will come.

Geoff Parling, the Leicester director of rugby, has come down from the stands and is fist-pumping his players and staff in their coaching area, as Tigers have the put-in at a scrum deep in their own half. Saints are powerless to influence things and Searle boots it out of play to the roars of a sold-out Welford Road.

The Tigers take home the bragging rights! It was a stodgy first half from both teams - but Leicester were arguably second best with their faltering lineout. Who would have thought they needed a good old half-time scuffle to refocus them? It was a near-perfect second half from Parling’s outfit, who are now three wins from four. As for Saints, they still can’t win at Welford Road.

Leicester get their lineout drive on and begin crabbing their way to the line. Taking off Henry Pollock for the extra heft of Callum Chick after 54 minutes was an understandable tactical move by Phil Dowson. It is a route one kind of a day.

But it probably does not do Pollock any favours in terms of pushing his case as a man for all seasons.

He didn’t do a lot wrong today but neither did he shine in the way that he - in more conducive conditions - is capable of.

The Leicester crowd were predictably delighted to wave him on his way.

Hamer-Webb ambushes Freeman with some force as the Saints man gathers Searle’s kick from deep after the restart. He’s penalised for holding on. Tigers don’t manage to capitilise on it

Smith finds Hendy out wide with a sumptous cross-field kick and the winger goes on the charge. He’s hauled down after about 20 metres but Radwan cyncially steps in his passing channel - he’s shown a yellow by Maxwell-Keys straight away.

Radwan is off.. or is he? The TMO has spotted a high hit from replacement lock Tom Lockett on Hamer-Webb in the build up to all of that.. and after a lengthy look Radwan’s yellow card is reversed and instead dished out to Lockett.

Tom Lockett sees yellow! 🟨 Direct head contact means @SaintsRugby will be a man down for the next 10 minutes 👀 📺 Stream TNT Sports on HBO Max https://t.co/ISqfkeU3vl https://t.co/IspWUcz3v5

Saints, eager to get back into this contest, enjoy a sustained period of pressure in Tigers’ 22. Hendy chases a Smith kick but there’s too much on it and he slides into the advertising hoardings. The winger seems okay, but the visitors will come back for a penalty. There’s some staunch resistance from Tigers - Heyes leads more celebrations in the faces of Saints’ players as the hosts regroup and win a penalty. Massive opportunity missed by Saints.

Oops, Saints leak a 17th penalty. Searle chucks an ambitious pass to Hamer-Webb, who in turn finds Wainwright out wide. The Welshman controls it exquisitely with a bit of footwork before being hauled to ground. Tigers are brought back for a pen, and Searle puts boot to ball in front of the posts. You feel Tigers have a bit of daylight now between their rivals.

That scrum before the Cameron Henderson try feels like a significant moment. There’s nothing a Welford Road full house likes to see more than an opposition pack on rollerskates at the set piece and that was Northampton in full retreat.

You could sense the psychological lift it gave Leicester and, on the back of the lineout drive try that kicked off the second half from Jamie Blamire, it feels like a hard road back for Northampton.

They’re not the champions for nothing, though.

The momentum is with Leicester now. The hosts come forward again and Searle tries to find Radwan out wide with a toe-poke but Steward is there to carry it into touch. Leicester aren’t done just yet - Blamire chucks in another clean arrow - and the forwards to do the rest.

Everybody on Saints’ tryline is expecting Heyes to pick-and-go but the prop catches them all by surprise by astutely popping it up to Carnduff, who bundles over.

It’s hasn’t been a good day from the tee for Searle, who misses another.

Play resumes and it’s a same Saints’ scrum, but Tigers get a huge shove on - Joe Heyes is in the thick of it - and the Tigers’ pack roar. The crowd loved that one.

The hosts kick to the corner, Blamire’s arrow is safely gathered by Henderson and the Tigers execute a superb training park move. Kata wins the collision and Heyes is among a number of decoy runners as JVP recycles quickly and the hosts spread it wide to Hamer-Webb, who finds Henderson on his outside. We have rugby again! Tigers go to the skies from the restart - Hamer-Webb gives chase - but doesn’t roll away and Saints wrestle back momentum, but can’t seem to sustain it and the hosts win it back. Steward does well to avoid being ambushed into touch - there’s a different intensity to the hosts this half, but neither side are having much luck keeping possession.

Pollock continues to give the hosts a headache, ripping the ball and Saints have the put-in at the scrum. The visitors ship it away quickly but play is stopped as Blamire, down injured, is attended to.

A 10-point match so far in rainy conditions - not much to write home about other than the confrontation before the break. Tigers begin on the front foot and win an offside penalty and for what seems like the umpteenth time in this match kick to the corner. Have they tidied up their lineout? They’ve kept this one as simple as possible with a short throw-in.

Kundiona is pernalised for a high tackle on JVP. Another penalty Tigers.. and this time they make it count! Throw, catch, drive and they’re over as Blamire finds his way to the line. It’s route one stuff. Searle can’t add the conversion.

Well, that was lively anyway. Full-scale conflagration to end a largely unwatchable half.

It was triggered by Alex Mitchell, of all people laughing, at Adam Radwan after he had been carried into touch in the final play of the half by George Hendy and Henry Pollock. Radwan took exception and from there things accelerated.

Leicester captain Ollie Chessum was at the heart of the pushing and shoving, snapping at Pollock in an argument that carried on with some pushing and shoving in the tunnel.

It gave the crowd something to get excited about after a poor 40 minutes.

Sometimes you get good games in bad conditions but this isn’t one of them.

Northampton have had the better of things but just when they look capable of getting their intricate interplay going there is a handling error.

Leicester’s defence, roared on with ‘Tigers, Tigers’ chants whenever the home side are on the back foot can take some credit for that.

They are still very much in this, four points adrift, but the tightness of the scoreline is the best that can be said for this contest so far.

More frustration from Tigers at the scrum, who fail to get the shove on. Mitchell senses it and delays his put-in ever so slightly and it works a treat. Saints are knocking on Tigers’ door and Fin Smith makes some good post-contact metres as he eats up grass and edges towards Tigers’ try line. Some staunch defence from the hosts, who survive after Prowse is penalised for not rolling away.

Steward lines up a kick from 50 metres and he splits the uprights. Tigers are on the board.

Craig Maxwell-Keys, the referee, won’t be short on advice this afternoon. Two penalties to Northampton and the home crowd are already growing restless.

He is going to need eyes in the back of his head this afternoon. It took all of two minutes for the first coming-together after a thumping double hit on Fin Smith from Archie van der Flier and Olly Cracknell.

There’s something heartening primal about an East Midlands derby and this one feels like it is right on the edge. It’s a sell-out and it is intense.

Henry Pollock’s cornrow phase is over. He’s sporting a mousy mop for today’s East Midlands derby.

The Northampton No 8 - currently warming up in a snood - will be pantomime-villain-in-chief for the Saints in these parts but he has a big afternoon ahead.

This is exactly the sort of occasion and arm wrestle which he needs to excel in to prove to Steve Borthwick he is worth more than a bench role for England next month.

Leicester were buoyed in the week by re-signing Jack van Poortfliet, who extended his contract with his boyhood club.

I grew up supporting Leicester, it’s always been my club,” said the England scrum half. This place feels like home in my rugby life. The club is in a really good position, I think we have a great group of lads and great coaches.

I love playing rugby here, I have my best mates here and I believe that we’ve got a group of lads that we can do great things with. I want to be in a place that I love playing for and I believe can win trophies.”

Squally conditions this afternoon at Mattioli Welford Road - in fact make that horrible. An interesting test then for Northampton as lovers of the beautiful game.

You would imagine that the rain and wind would suit a Leicester side whose DNA is set piece power better.

Expect the catch and drive to get plenty of game time and Jack van Poortvliet and Billy Searle to go to the air regularly. It could be a stern examination for teenage Saints full-back James Pater.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the new campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

Tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back quickly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” said Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

Kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.
